events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.
events.title: refractiv Photography Exhibition

As citizens invested in hope for a future built on love and care, we know that the next generation requires our attention to nourish them into becoming the compassionate, responsible, and thoughtful humans the next chapter of humanity needs. The works in this show feature images centering play, connection, and collaboration as enriching elements of young people's lives. The artists: Sasha Wilk, Gabe Wolfe, Kyra Watkins, Elizabeth Goss, Stefania Salles Bruins, Corinne Kenly Barber, Forest Salazar, Danny Stephens and Kristie Winther. events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

events.summary: Shadow work is about facing the parts of yourself you usually avoid: the fears, doubts, and emotions you’ve buried. It’s not about judging them but understanding where they come from and how they shape you. When you bring these hidden parts into the light, you free yourself from old patterns and grow into a more authentic version of yourself. Each month, we will gather in community to meet our shadows with compassion, curiosity, and gentle awareness. Together, we will create a safe and supportive space to explore the parts of ourselves that often remain hidden - the emotions, patterns, beliefs, and experiences that are asking to be witnessed, understood, and integrated. During this two-hour healing experience, we will move through personal reflection, guided meditation, and community connection. Through guided shadow work prompts, journaling and community discussion, we will explore various themes with kindness for ourselves and for others. Guided meditation will help us connect internally, followed by community discussion and sharing (always optional) to remind us that we are not alone in our healing journeys. We will close with a grounding sound bath to fully integrate our deep work and rebalance the nervous system before we part ways. Each month will offer a new theme for exploration. Jess Spain holds a B.S. in Psychology and a minor in Child and Family Studies from Portland State University. Before COVID, she worked as a counselor for several years, with a focus on serving the Indigenous community in her area. During that time, she developed her own group curriculum centered on mindfulness, DBT skills, and emotional intelligence. Jess is a Portland, Oregon Indigenous (Cow Creek Umpqua enrolled) spiritualist, Reiki Usui Master, mindfulness teacher, and astrologer. Her esoteric journey began in childhood and has continued to grow into an integral part of who she is today. She is a Level 2 Reiki practitioner, sound healer, and certified 200-hour yoga instructor. Jess has been a formal meditation student since 2020, with ongoing training and education in mindfulness and meditation. In 2021, she attended Nightlight Astrology School, where she studied Hellenistic Astrology. She has found deep joy in exploring birth charts alongside healing work and using astrology as a tool to guide and support others. Two Moons Wellness is Jess’s way of bringing together her culture, educational background, and esoteric studies into one practice—uniting body, mind, and spirit with universal flow. She believes in the transformative power of introspection, including shadow work, grounded in mindfulness, to help others connect more deeply with their higher selves. Jess has applied these practices to her own life through mindfulness training and experienced a sense of inner peace, tranquility, and serenity she once did not believe possible. Through Two Moons Wellness, she hopes to share these transformative tools with others and help them discover greater peace in this life. One of her greatest teachers said, “The only way out is in.”
events.title: Two Moons: Monthly Shadow Work Immersion ANGER with Jess Spain

events.summary: From bayou kitchens to front porches, this captivating play celebrates the heart, humor, and resilience of Louisiana's women. Pull up a chair and savor a celebration of the remarkable women whose strength and spirit have always been the secret ingredient in Louisiana’s gumbo. This show is for you if you’ve ever wondered… Where do I belong? Where is home? What is a Cajun? What’s a Creole? Are they more than just styles of cooking? How different are Southerners from Northwesterners? How do you make a roux? What’s Mardi Gras all about anyway? What’s the deal with New Orleans and voodoo, vampires, and above ground graves? How do you “laissez les bon temps rouler”? Can you be both proud and ashamed of where you come from? How do you pronounce geaux, lagniappe, Ouachita, Tchoupitoulas, or couillon? Do you know what it means to miss New Orleans? Shelley Tate's one-woman show developed as an ensemble piece: a 90-minute show about history and culture of Louisiana —served with heart, humor, and just the right amount of spice. The gumbo is rich, the laughter is loud, and the women are unforgettable. events.summary: Do You Feel Anger? lives in the familiar world of water coolers, staplers, and office conference rooms — but Nelson-Greenberg's language quickly reveals something far stranger underneath. When Sofia, an empathy coach, arrives at a debt collection agency as part of a lawsuit settlement, she finds a workplace where toxic masculinity has so thoroughly warped the atmosphere that even the most basic concepts — feelings, empathy, basic human decency — have become alien and absurd. The play is laugh-out-loud funny, populated by an unusual cast of characters whose skewed logic and bizarre non-sequiturs mask something genuinely unsettling. What emerges from the sensitivity training sessions is not reform, but a portrait of how pervasive and deeply embedded the patriarchy can be — and how it distorts everyone it touches, including those trying to resist it.

events.summary: See Jane Run, An Indo Story is a solo memoir play written and performed by Dr. Jane Vogel Mantiri and directed by Andrés Alcalá. Step into the powerful, true story of an Indo (Indonesian-European) refugee child who grows up to reclaim her voice, her history, and her joy. In this intimate, one‑woman show, Jane traces her journey from wartime displacement and family silence to healing, humor, and hard‑won hope, inviting audiences to consider what it really means to belong. There will be a brief talkback after the show. All Ages $15-$20/person sliding Scale. See Jane Run is a riveting, raw, and funny refugee immigrant story about the flawed pursuit of the American Dream. Jane takes audiences on a fast-paced and eye-opening journey from her homeland in Indonesia to the United States. Papa tells Jane, “We will all be happy in America. I promise!” As the family flees danger, the trauma and secrets of the past follow them, and their odyssey is filled with unexpected twists and turns. Dr. Jane Vogel Mantiri is a retired trauma psychologist, acclaimed Portland actor, social justice activist, and founder of AGE: Advance Gender and Equity in the Arts. Acting credits include Children’s Hour, Speech and Debate, Clean House, and Fred’s Mom in Portlandia. She founded Advance Gender Equity in the Arts (AGE), a Portland-based social justice arts organization created to empower artists who have been marginalized because of gender, age, and race. Jane was awarded the 2025 Distinguished Alumni Award by her alma mater, Carroll University. Drawing on a lifetime of advocacy and artistry, she brings the “American Indo Dream” to life with raw honesty, warmth, and unexpected laughter. Andrés Alcalá is a national award winning actor, director, educator, and teaching artist. He has performed in numerous theaters including the Oregon Shakespeare Festival, Portland Center Stage, Artist Repertory Theatre, Northwest Children's Theatre, Arizona Theatre Company, Phoenix Theatre, as well as six years as an associate artist with Childsplay. He has performed in two National Tours, and directed and performed as Ferdinand the Bull on the National Tour. Andrés holds a BFA in acting from Southern Oregon University. He has spent the last 15 years developing his skills as an animation and projection designer for theatre. In addition to being a multi-hypenate artist, Andrés enjoys living life on the road, and spending as much time with his immediate family as possible. He is choosing to focus on artistic work that has a heart.
events.title: See Jane Run, An Indo Story (Theater Production)

events.summary: Unseen captures a ceremonial expedition through Oregon’s most remote wilderness, where invisible wounds meet invincible spirit. As these veterans bikepack across rugged terrain, they carry more than gear—they carry stories of trauma, resilience, and the right to roam freely, without hate, prejudice, or silence. The journey begins in Lakeview, Oregon—a quiet, intimate town known as the gateway to the Oregon Timber Trail the last frontier. From this sacred starting point, the veterans launch the Freedom to Roam project: a 200-mile odyssey through ancestral lands, volcanic plateaus, and alpine forests. The Oregon Timber Trail is more than a route—it’s a living corridor of history and healing. Stretching over 600 miles from California to the Columbia River Gorge, it invites all people to explore, reflect, and reconnect with nature on their own terms. It is open to everyone, regardless of background, identity, or burden. This film honors the legacy of the Triple Nickel —America’s first Black smokejumpers, who protected Oregon’s forests during World War II when they were denied the right to fight. Their story echoes through the trees, as today’s veterans pick up the torch of remembrance and ride toward justice. Unseen is not just a film. It is a movement. A prayer. A trail toward healing.
events.title: UNSEEN: A Documentary Screening

events.summary: Run Time: 105 min. TICKETS $15 Doors 3:30 p.m.; Event 4 p.m. Select Showtime to Purchase Tickets Click here to learn more about accessibility at the Tomorrow Theater. THE EXPERIENCE Join us for a very special Portland premiere of director Chad Brown's new documentary Unseen: Invisible Wounds, Invincible Spirit. Taking place the week of Veterans Day, this film follows five veterans as they bike through two hundred miles of raw, unforgiving wilderness on a trail that asks everything of you and gives back something no clinic or desk job ever could. Following the film, director Chad Brown will be joined on stage for a Q&A about the film. ON SCREEN: Unseen 2026. Directed by Chad Brown. Runtime: 65 minutes. They came to Lakeview, Oregon, carrying things that don't fit in a pack. Five veterans. Two hundred miles of raw, unforgiving wilderness. One trail that asks everything of you and gives back something no clinic or desk job ever could. Unseen begins at the edge of what most people call the end of the map Lakeview, Oregon, the last frontier, the quiet gateway to the Oregon Timber Trail; from that threshold, it launches something that can only be called a reckoning. This is not an adventure film. This is a document of survival, of spirits refusing to be broken, of invisible wounds meeting invincible will. Five veterans strap into their bikes and ride into the kind of silence that forces you to finally hear yourself. The cameras go with them. And what unfolds over volcanic plateaus, through alpine forests and ancestral lands, across a living corridor of history that stretches 600 miles from the California border to the Columbia River Gorge is something that will not let you look away. But Unseen is not only the story of these five riders. It is haunted by another story one America nearly buried. The Triple Nickel. The 555th Parachute Infantry Battalion. America's first Black smokejumpers, who were dispatched to Oregon's forests during World War II on a covert mission called Operation Firefly protecting this very land from Japanese incendiary balloon bombs at a time when their country denied them the right to fight as combat soldiers overseas. They parachuted into burning forests to save a nation that had not yet decided to save them. Their bravery was classified. Their names, forgotten. Their sacrifice, erased. Today, as five veterans pedal through the same wilderness those men protected with their lives, their ghosts ride alongside. The Oregon Timber Trail becomes something more than a route. It becomes a corridor of memory. A long-overdue act of remembrance. A very special thank you to Senator Ron Wyden for his support of the film. Thank You to the following sponsors - GRAYL, Oregon Film, Sawyer, Snow Peak, Travel Oregon, Gossamer Gear, and Gear Squatch. ON STAGE: Chad Brown \(Director\) - Chad Brown is an award-winning photographer, filmmaker, Navy veteran, and conservationist whose work fuses visual storytelling with advocacy for wild places and underrepresented communities. As founder of Soul River Inc. and Love Is King, he champions BIPOC and Indigenous voices while leading Arctic expeditions and national conservation efforts. His upcoming films, Unseen and Exposure, debut in November 2026, continuing his mission to inspire action, elevate unheard voices, and protect the wild spaces shaping our collective future. OM
events.title: Unseen: Invisible Wounds, Invincible Spirit

events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.
events.title: Sunday Yoga: Foundations and Flow

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Join PSU professor and violinist Tomás Cotik and pianist Shinmyung Rho for an evening celebrating some of the most captivating works in the French violin repertoire. The program features the elegance and imagination of Claude Debussy’s Violin Sonata, the lyrical charm of Lili Boulanger’s Nocturne and Cortège, the expressive intensity of Francis Poulenc’s Violin Sonata, and two beloved works by Maurice Ravel: the Violin Sonata No. 2 and the dazzling virtuoso showpiece Tzigane. Spanning the late Romantic and early modern eras, these works reveal the remarkable palette of colors, textures, and emotions that characterizes French music, showcasing its refinement, imagination, and brilliance.

events.summary: In two decades on the road Jeffrey Foucault has become one of the most distinctive voices in American music, refining a sound instantly recognizable for its simplicity and emotional power. With a string of critically acclaimed studio albums – “Stark, literate songs that are as wide open as the landscape of his native Midwest” \(The New Yorker\), "Beat-up troubadour folk whittled to dolorous perfection” \(Uncut\), “Songwriting Brilliance,” \(Irish Times\) – he’s built a brick-and-mortar international touring career and a devoted following that includes luminaries like Van Dyke Parks, Greil Marcus, Gregory Alan Isakov, and Don Henley. In September of 2024 Jeffrey Foucault released THE UNIVERSAL FIRE \(Fluff & Gravy, 9/6/24\), his first album of entirely new material since 2018. A series of high-voltage performances cut live in one room, the album is both a working wake – Foucault lost his best friend and drummer Billy Conway, to cancer in 2021 – and a meditation on the nature of beauty, artifact, and loss. Augmenting Foucault's all-star band with members of Calexico and Bon Iver \(drummer John Convertino and producer/saxophonist Mike Lewis\) THE UNIVERSAL FIRE sets Conway’s death against the massive 2008 fire at the Universal Studios lot in California that destroyed the masters of certain bedrock American recordings, to interrogate ideas about mortality, legacy, meaning, and calling.
events.title: Jeffrey Foucault

events.summary: World Vegan Month 2026 Vegan Specials For A Cause All Month Long Presented by Veganizer, World Vegan Month is back for its fourth year! From November 1 to November 30, enjoy delicious food and drink specials at 35 participating businesses, from restaurants and bakeries to food carts and popups. Enjoy vegan specials for a cause all month long. Collect stamps to complete a stamp card for a chance to win gift cards. A portion of sales from every special will be donated to a cause chosen by that business. Together, we will be supporting a variety of causes, including humanitarian, cultural, environmental, animal, equity and justice organizations. World Vegan Month was founded in November 1994 to mark The Vegan Society's 50th anniversary. Today, World Vegan Month is celebrated worldwide to recognize the vegan movement and vegan communities all over. events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

Beth Wood is an award-winning songwriter, poet, joyful singer, teacher, and believer in the power of word and song. Beth has been writing, performing, and creating for over thirty years — delighting and inspiring audiences with her exceptional musicianship, intelligent writing, powerhouse voice, and warm and commanding stage presence. Beth has released sixteen albums, four books of poetry, and a collection of funny stories from the road. In 2018, she reached her goal of playing in all fifty states. Beth is a co-founder of She’s Speaking, a collective that creates forums/spaces for women’s voices and stories to be heard. Beth is guided by her mission of nurturing connection, creativity, and belonging through music and poetry. Her work has expanded to include teaching and song coaching as well as leading and facilitating workshops, classes, and retreats. She is the director of the Sisters Folk Festival Americana Song Academy, a three-and-a-half day songwriting retreat in Sisters, OR. She lives in Sisters with her dog Hannah Laroo. Learn more at bethwoodmusic.com patreon.com/bethwoodmusic Cal Scott is an award-winning singer-songwriter, musician, multi instrumentalist and composer, Scott has scored more than 50 documentaries and specials for PBS. His theme for Oregon Experience is heard weekly on Oregon Public Broadcasting. He has toured and recorded with Irish fiddler Kevin Burke, and for 25 years was the musical director of the The Trail Band. Their new music video for the song, Midnight Drive, has received six awards from Film festivals, including Best Music Video, Oregon Independent Film Festival, 2023. Richard Moore has been playing music since "The Wombats" in high school. Traveled through Europe and Thailand in the '70's in a rock and roll band. Settled down in Portland in the '80's and built a recording studio...Tag Team Audio...where he engineered commercial audio projects for 40 years. He was the voice of Pacific Power on their commercials...and still is if you get put on hold. Richard came back to music midlife, and performed regularly with his old friend Cal Scott at O'Connors in Multnomah Village where they hosted a local songwriter round for 12 years. He’s been writing songs his whole life and just finished producing his 5th and...final..? CD of original tunes....FLOW. He could be the best songwriter you’ve never heard of.

events.summary: For forty years, Farm Sanctuary has been at the forefront of efforts to raise awareness and end factory farming abuses. It started a movement to change how society views and treats farm animals and to transform the lives of humans and other animals. Founded as an all-volunteer grassroots effort in 1986, it was originally funded by selling vegan hotdogs outside Grateful Dead concerts. Its pioneering investigations exposed egregious cruelty to farm animals and led to animal rescues, starting with Hilda, a sheep who was discarded on a pile of dead animals behind a stockyard. Along with operating farms and caring for rescued animals, the organization has developed groundbreaking education and advocacy efforts, engaged with dignitaries and celebrities, and passed the first US laws to restrict factory farming cruelty. Farm Sanctuary's work has been widely covered in media outlets, including The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Wall Street Journal, The Los Angeles Times, Newsweek, Time, NPR, ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN, Fox, and many others. It is internationally recognized, and its work has inspired individuals and organizations around the globe. Co-founder Gene Baur’s Farm Sanctuary: The Story of a Movement \(Lantern Publishing\) offers an inspiring testament to the power of kindness and action, encouraging readers to consider their own choices and join the movement toward a more just and humane world for everyone. A powerful retrospective that chronicles Farm Sanctuary's humble beginnings in 1986 to its leading role in the fight for ethical, sustainable, and compassionate food systems, Farm Sanctuary features powerful images, personal reflections from activists and supporters, and moving commentary on the evolving and life-changing landscape of animal agriculture. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/gene-baur-9781590567555
events.title: Powell's Presents: Gene Baur

events.summary: Since the team’s founding in 1976, the Seattle Mariners have become one of the most important social institutions in Seattle. Beginning with the brief tenure of the Seattle Pilots and the legal battle with MLB to bring baseball back to the city, the early years were a struggle, as were the 1980s. In 1989 Ken Griffey Jr. made his debut and established himself as one of the most talented players of his era. The Mariners had their first season above .500 in 1991 and then moved into their most successful years in team history. Led by manager Lou Piniella and future Hall of Famers Edgar Martinez, Griffey Jr., and Randy Johnson, the Mariners won their first division title in 1995 and defeated the New York Yankees in dramatic fashion in game 5 of the American League Division Series, one of the most iconic moments in team history. When voters had rejected an earlier vote to build the team a new stadium to replace the Kingdome, the state legislature seized on the team’s momentum to build a new stadium that would ensure their place in the Northwest forever. In 2001 rookie player Ichiro Suzuki led the team to an MLB record of 116-46 and won both the American League MVP and Rookie of the Year awards. While the team struggled for most of its fifty-year run, new management in the front office and a retooled farm system got the Mariners into the playoffs in 2022 and again in 2025, where they fell just short of the World Series. In You Gotta Love These Guys \(University of Nebraska Press\), David F. Schmitz recounts the full history of the Seattle Mariners, covering the team on the field, the larger history off the field, and the team’s impact as a social institution on Seattle and the Pacific Northwest. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/david-f-schmitz-9781496240576
events.title: Powell's Presents: David F. Schmitz

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/FE26 On Sale Thursday, May 21st at 10am PT \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ Fred Eaglesmith has played them all; from television’s The Late Show with David Letterman to the legendary Grand Ole Opry in Nashville to the refined acoustics of the Lincoln Center, but this fall, Canada’s most uncompromising troubadour brings his whip-smart songwriting and road-tested show back to the very communites that inspired him. And you won’t want to miss it. The Juno Award winning poet of rural Canada has spent four decades turning service station stories, county fair romances, broken down old tractors, and gravel roads into timeless songs. His devoted fan base, affectionately known as ‘Fred Heads’ and a reputation for delivering shows that are equal parts intimate and electrifying have established this founder of alt-country as the benchmark for his contemporaries as well as aspiring artists. Eaglesmith’s songs, filled with wit, heart, and unvarnished truth have been covered by the likes of Alan Jackson, Toby Keith, Miranda Lambert and countless others. Over 120 artists from Bluegrass to Punk have recorded his popular tune, “Alcohol & Pills.” His hit, “Trucker Speed,” has been named to the 100 Top Americana Songs of All Time and garnered over 60 million views with over 6 thousand independent videos having been created on Tik Tok. For the last 15 years,Eaglesmith has been joined by Texas-born, multi-instrumentalist, Tif Ginn, who also happens to be his wife. Together they have developed a musical symbiosis that only comes from countless miles, shared stages and an undenyable chemistry. And now with the addition of their band, which includes their 16 year old, 30 year old songs land like fresh revelations and new tunes take shape in real time. Eaglesmith carries the weight of a legend lightly. After a lifetime of touring and 25 albums under his belt he’d have every right to rest on his laurels. Instead, he’s doing what he’s always done: pointing the truck toward Canada’s backroads, where the next great night of music waits to be sparked. His signature sound of country soul & rock energy with his between-song tales only he can tell- equally hilarious & heartbreaking, make the Fred Eaglesmith Show unmatched. Fred doesn’t just perform in these small towns, he plugs into their heartbeat-after all these years, that’s still his superpower
events.title: Fred Eaglesmith

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

events.summary: Grammy-winning Mexican guitar duo Rodrigo y Gabriela return with OurHome, a bold new album and global tour that invites audiences into a dreamlike universe of rogue monsters, celestial birds, stardust, savage landscapes, and the search for inner peace. Self-produced in Tokyo, OurHome is both a love letter to Japan and a meditation on what it means to find home within yourself, delivered through the wildly expressive instrumental guitar music that has made Rodrigo Sánchez and Gabriela Quintero one of the most electrifying live acts in the world. For more than two decades, Rodrigo y Gabriela have pushed acoustic guitar into new territory, blending classical, rock, metal, cinematic atmosphere, and spiritual exploration into a sound entirely their own. From their early days busking on Dublin’s Grafton Street, they have gone on to win a GRAMMY Award for Mettavolution, headline Glastonbury, and sell out iconic stages including the Hollywood Bowl, Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Royal Albert Hall, Radio City Music Hall, and the Sydney Opera House. On OurHome, the duo returns to the textural beauty of acoustic instrumentation while expanding their world with guests including Marty Friedman and Hiromi. Live, Rodrigo’s lightning-fast lead lines and Gabriela’s hypnotic, hard-hitting rhythms become a pulse-raising journey of stillness, intensity, and unstoppable momentum. For longtime fans and first-timers alike, this is a rare chance to experience two master musicians at their most adventurous, intimate, and powerful.

events.summary: Searching for a plot for his next legal thriller, D.C. area lawyer and novelist Michael Harris stumbles across a conspiracy theory that may have put his own life at risk. Five years ago, Gloria Hale, the President's wife, was assassinated by a lone gunman, who was himself killed in a shootout with a security guard while trying to escape. At the same time and hotel, a young lawyer, Marsha Hart, disappears in the chaos after the shooting, only to have her murdered body turn up a few days later, her murder never solved. Michael Harris is a D. C. area lawyer with a second career as a novelist, but after a very successful debut, his subsequent legal thrillers have been less and less successful. With one more book due under his contract and desperate to revive his flagging career, Harris is stumbles across the voluminous research done by a recently deceased former Secret Service agent obsessed with proving that the First Lady's assassination was a conspiracy. Thinking he might be able to turn one of these wildly unlikely theories into his next book, Harris begins to look into the matter. He doesn't turn up anything but his inquiries might have set something into motion — leading to another murder, a fire destroying the original evidence, and an attempt assault of Harris himself. This might be a coincidence or Harris may well be the next target in an increasingly deadly conspiracy. Conspiracy Theory \(Minotaur\) is the new thriller from Phillip Margolin, author of False Witness and An Insignificant Case. His new book, A Giant Leap: How AI is Transforming Healthcare — and What That Means for Our Future, is a guide to how today's technological revolution is reshaping how all of us, from patients to clinicians, experience healthcare. A Bold Vision for Healthcare's AI Revolution Across every major industry, artificial intelligence has proven to be a powerful tool in improving systems and scaling impact. As this tech rapidly integrates into clinical settings, it brings both extraordinary promise and significant concerns about hallucinations, bias and misinformation. Dr. Robert Wachter shares his visionary perspective on how AI is already matching — and sometimes surpassing — physicians in critical areas from diagnostic accuracy to patient empathy. With clear-eyed optimism and actionable insights, he argues that AI will have a profound, positive impact on healthcare if we navigate its implementation thoughtfully.

events.summary: The Residents are an avant-garde/experimental music and visual arts group heavily influenced by Dada and largely shrouded in mystery and myth. The Residents began recording in 1969, although many of these recordings from their early years have still gone unreleased to this day \(the earliest material from The Residents, traded among bootlegs, "The Warner Brothers Tape" and "Baby Sex", were both recorded in 1971\). The Residents first official release, "Santa Dog", was released in 1972. Allmusic had this to say about The Residents: "Over the course of a recording career spanning several decades, the Residents remained a riddle of Sphinx-like proportions; cloaking their lives and music in a haze of willful obscurity, the band's members never identified themselves by name, always appearing in public in disguise -- usually tuxedos, top hats and giant eyeball masks -- and refusing to grant media interviews. Drawing inspiration from the likes of fellow innovators including Harry Partch, Sun Ra, and Captain Beefheart, the Residents channelled the breadth of American music into their idiosyncratic, satiric vision, their mercurial blend of electronics, distortion, avant-jazz, classical symphonies and gratingly nasal vocals reinterpreting everyone from John Philip Sousa to James Brown while simultaneously expanding the boundaries of theatrical performance and multimedia interaction. It was commonly accepted that the four-member group emigrated to San Francisco, California from Shreveport, Louisiana at some point in the early '70s. According to longtime group spokesman Jay Clem -- one member of the so-called Cryptic Corporation, the band's representative body -- they received their name when Warner Bros. mailed back their anonymous demo tape, addressed simply "for the attention of residents." Finding no takers for their oddball sounds, the Residents founded their own label, Ralph Records, for the purposes of issuing their 1972 debut "Santa Dog," released in a pressing of 300 copies which were mailed out to luminaries from Frank Zappa to President Richard Nixon. Their debut full-length, 1974's Meet the Residents, reportedly sold fewer than 50 copies before the group was threatened with a lawsuit from Capitol Records over its cover, a twisted, dada-esque parody of the art to Meet the Beatles. The follow-up, 1974's neo-classical excursion Not Available, was recorded with the intention of its music remaining unissued; locked in cold storage upon its completion, only a 1978 contractual obligation resulted in its eventual release. 1976's Third Reich 'N' Roll was the next official offering, a collection of pop oldies covers presented in a controversial jacket portraying Adolf Hitler clutching an enormous carrot. After a 1976 concert in Berkeley, California which cloaked the Residents behind an opaque screen, wrapped up like mummies -- the most famous of only three live performances mounted during their first decade of existence -- they issued an abrasive 1977 cover of the Rolling Stones' "Satisfaction," which became an underground hit on both sides of the Atlantic at the peak of the punk movement. As the decade drew to a close, the group released a flurry of recordings, further building upon their growing cult following; among them were 1977's Duck Stab/Buster & Glen, 1979's Eskimo \(purportedly a collection of native Arctic chants\) and 1980's Commercial Album, a compilation of 40 one-minute "pop songs" that aired on San Francisco radio only because the Residents played them during the advertising time they bought. In 1981 the Residents embarked upon their "Mole Trilogy," a prog rock collection of albums -- 1981's The Mark of the Mole, 1982's The Tunes of Two Cities and 1985's The Big Bubble -- recounting an epic battle between a pair of tribes named the Moles and the Chubs; a lavish, multimedia tour, "The Mole Show," followed. In the interim, the group also mounted another ambitious project, the "American Composer" series, although only two of the projected titles -- 1984's George and James \(a reinterpretation of songs by George Gershwin and James Brown\) and 1986's Stars and Hank Forever \(celebrating John Philip Sousa and Hank Williams\) -- ever appeared. Instead, in the wake of financial and corporate difficulties which resulted in the creation of a New Ralph label, the Residents issued the one-off God in Three Persons \(a talking blues outing\), and 1989's The King and Eye \(a reinterpretation of Elvis Presley standards\). After losing control of the Ralph label as well as their back catalog, the Residents regained the rights to their music in 1990 and began reissuing long-out-of-print material as well as the new Freak Show, a meditation on circus sideshows and carnival dementia. Four years later, Freak Show was reissued as a CD-ROM, marking the group's first leap into the new digital interactive technology; Have a Bad Day followed in 1996, and included the soundtrack to the CD-ROM game "Bad Day on the Midway." In 1997, the band celebrated their silver anniversary with the release of the career-spanning overview Our Tired, Our Poor, Our Huddled Masses. Wormwood: Curious Stories From the Bible followed the next year, with Roadworms \(songs from Wormwood as performed in the stage show\) being issued in mid-2000. They followed that up with the awesome Icky Flix DVD, an incredibly detailed collection of their videos that featured both old and new soundtracks, 5.1 Digital Stereo Surround sound, countless hidden videos and in-depth histories of each individual track. That was followed by another one of their rare tours, which saw them incorporate the DVD into their live act and bring out guest singer Molly Harvey for some truly creative duets. The Petting Zoo retrospective followed in the spring of 2002, acting as a budget sampler for new fans and giving old fans something to tide them over while several high concept projects neared completion. The first was Demons Dance Alone, a complicated pop album that hearkened back to the catchier material from Duck Stab and The Commercial Album. That was followed in 2002 by a live retrospective called Kettles of Fish on the Outskirts of Town that contained 3 cd's and a DVD, and a further look at their past via remasters and remixes put out by EuroRalph \(including a remix of their previously unreleased and notorious "Warner Brothers Demo"\). A DVD of the Demons Dance Alone tour came out in 2004 and another new project, Animal Lover was released in 2005."

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: City Councilors Angelita Morillo and Jamie Dunphy will host Portland-based youth organization Outside The Frame for a screening of films written, directed, and produced by local youth who have experienced homelessness. The event will take place Wednesday, November 18 at 4:30 PM at the Portland City Hall Atrium, 1221 SW 4th Avenue. The event is free and open to the public, with filmmakers in attendance. “These films express hard-earned truths,” said Nili Yosha, Executive Director of Outside The Frame. “Screening them at City Hall, where decisions profoundly impact the lives of homeless youth, celebrates the insight and talents of the filmmakers while restoring a sense of dignity and possibility." The screening program will highlight Outside The Frame’s model educational and vocational program, which operates on the foundational belief that young people need more than their basic needs met to thrive. Participants create films about issues that matter to them and share them with the public. “Outside the Frame empowers people to act within their own agency and to do things that are creative and beautiful and organic,” said program participant Monet Wilds. “More than just something to chew on. More than just somewhere to be. Outside the Frame is doing something for our souls; they're giving us something for our hearts. Outside the Frame programs inspire you, grow you, love you.” “Outside the Frame opens so many doors for people,” said Carmelo Cherastil, who traveled to the Friday Harbor Film Festival in Washington last month to screen his directorial debut. “I've never looked back to being on the street and I just keep making movies.” “It’s one of a kind,” said Lucius Lowe, a participant in Outside the Frame’s flagship three week film intensive program. “I haven't seen anything like it. It's very helpful. It builds confidence for people. It’s a real opportunity to gain resume experience and make money.” The featured films on the City Hall program offer a direct look into the lives of a population where BIPOC, LGBTQ\+ youth, and people with disabilities are disproportionately over-represented. Event Schedule: 4:30 PM: Doors open and refreshments served \(Portland City Hall Atrium\) 5:00 PM: OTF Screening program begins 6:00 PM: Special ceremony at Council Chambers Outside The Frame is a Portland-based non-profit organization providing a creative outlet, job training, and a sense of dignity to youth experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity through the art of filmmaking. Learn more at outsidetheframe.org
events.title: Outside the Frame Films at City Hall

events.summary: Gina Saputo with George Mitchell \(p\), Phil Baker\(b\), & Charlie Doggett\(d\) Portland’s love affair with jazz is being rekindled in truly iconic fashion. Beginning September 17, 2025, The Benson Hotel proudly unveils The Benson Jazz Revival — a free weekly jazz series that brings smooth sounds, community connection, and cultural vibrancy back to the heart of downtown. Hosted every Wednesday from 5–7 PM in the hotel’s elegant lobby lounge, the series will showcase a dynamic mix of the Pacific Northwest’s top jazz talent, emerging artists, and surprise special guests. Seating is first come, first served — arrive early to secure the best spot. Crafted in collaboration with nonprofit partner Elevate Unity Inc., The Benson Jazz Revival is about more than music — it’s a celebration of community, connection, and shared experience. Elevate Unity’s mission reflects the heart of the series: to bring people together through unity, inclusiveness, and a love of culture. Guests can expect an immersive evening that blends the richness of Portland’s jazz heritage with elevated craft beverages including Don Julio, Bulleit, Ketel One, Rendition Rye, Kur Gin, and local favorite Dobbes Family Winery, and a rotating selection of chef-inspired hors d’oeuvres — all set within one of the city’s most storied venues. “Our mission is to breathe new life into downtown through the power of jazz, hospitality, and community connection,” says Ryan Kunzer, Managing Director of The Benson Hotel. “The Benson Jazz Revival isn’t just about music — it’s about rebuilding and celebrating Portland’s diverse creative spirit.” Supported by a growing roster of cultural partners and sponsors — including Jack London Revue, The Portland Skanner, Soul’d Out Productions, and MusicPortland — the series serves as a vibrant call to return downtown and rediscover the energy that makes Portland unforgettable. As the city continues its resurgence, The Benson Jazz Revival offers a joyful reminder that when music, people, and place come together, magic happens. Event Details • Launch Date: September 17, 2025 • When: Every Wednesday, 5–7 PM • Where: Lobby Lounge, The Benson Hotel • Admission: Free & Open to the Public • Food/Drink: Available for purchase

events.summary: Description This month join us at the Tucker Maxon School! In 1947, teacher Alice Maxon declared "deaf people can learn to talk," and with a financial investment from philanthropist Max Tucker, she and five families establish a school teaching exactly that. Today, Tucker Maxon School's mission is to teach deaf and hearing children to listen, talk, learn, and achieve excellence together. The crux of our mission is to empower children to thrive when they move on to middle school and beyond. We accomplish that by ensuring that every child - regardless of ability - has been given the communication and literacy tools they need to prosper in the classroom as well as the social resiliency to thrive through adolescence. In a mainstream school environment, Tucker Maxon provides wraparound services to deaf and hard of hearing children, including speech-language pathology, clinical audiology, and teachers of the deaf. Students have regular access to these services that would otherwise be intermittent and require extra time out of the classroom.

Choose from a variety of delicious tea to sip on while practicing tasseomancy \(tea leaf reading\) with longtime tea leaf reader & herbalist Ciaran Keast! Date: Wednesday, November 18th Event: 5:30 - 6:30 PM PDT Location: Seagrape Apothecary - 2823 NE Sandy Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97232. In this hour long gathering, we'll dive into the realm of magic, tea leaf reading & self-care with like-minded babes in a cozy and welcoming atmosphere. Some helpful tea practices to explore prior to the workshop ☕ \(if you have time\): Get to know your tea! Smell it and notice all the aromas. Touch the cup to your lips and notice the warmth and texture. events.summary: Few conservation behaviors have captured the public's interest as much as recycling. But sorting your trash and placing it at the curb isn't recycling . . . it's just the start of a long and somewhat surprising journey for your empty milk cartons and back issues of Cat Fancy. Where do those materials go once in the bin? How do they get sorted out? And where do they go from there? What about those rumors that recycling trucks just deliver materials to the landfill, or dump them in the ocean? How can recycling even deliver environmental benefit, given all of the trucks and machinery involved? What's the deal with plastic, anyway? You have questions, and we have answers! After pioneering recycling policy in the late 1980s, Oregon is now implementing the first "extended producer responsibility" law for packaging in the U.S. The Plastic Pollution and Recycling Modernization Act, adopted in 2021, was launched July 1, 2025 and is designed to provide residents and businesses a recycling system that can be trusted to deliver the environmental benefits that recycling has long promised. But even a fully modernized recycling system has limited potential to stem the tide of unsustainable levels of production and consumption. Explore how recycling is simultaneously necessary and insufficient, how recycling needs to be improved, and what else Oregon could be doing to use materials sustainably. David Allaway and Justin Gast work at the OR Department of Environmental Quality, and between them have over 57 years of experience with recycling systems. In addition to his time at DEQ, Justin has worked at the local and national levels for the likes of Resource Recycling magazine, the Washington County \(OR\) Solid Waste & Recycling Program and The Recycling Partnership. David has testified before Congress and co-chaired Oregon's Recycling Steering Committee, and his work has been featured in Last Week Tonight with John Oliver, the National Law Review, Time, Sierra and PBS Frontline. Minors ok when accompanied by a parent or guardian Review our venue FAQ here ALL SALES ARE FINAL. PLEASE, DOUBLE CHECK YOUR ORDER BEFORE PURCHASING. NO REFUNDS.

events.summary: Orkney \(Scotland\) born fiddler Louise Bichan and Indiana \(USA\) mandolinist Ethan Setiawan present a collaboration and meeting of their musical worlds in Hildaland. A path steeped in the fiddle traditions of their respective sides of the Atlantic, the journey taken wends through Scottish, oldtime, and Swedish inspired music intertwined with contemporary compositions. Bichan’s fiddle is a melodic foil to Setiawan’s counterpoint and harmonic depth, and the two weave in and out seamlessly. Setiawan has won such accolades as the 2014 National Mandolin Championship, the 2017 RockyGrass Mandolin Championship and has shared the stage with the likes of Julian Lage, Darrell Scott, Bryan Sutton, Mike Marshall, Tony Trischka, Darol Anger, Casey Driessen, the Steel Wheels, Don Stiernberg, Matt Flinner, and Jacob Jolliff. Bichan has won awards for her compositions and playing, and has travelled far and wide to perform in various line ups since a young age. She has appeared at the likes of the BBC TV's Hogmanay Live show, Edinburgh Castle, Reading Festival, Cambridge Folk Festival, Lorient Interceltique Festival, Milwaukee Irish Festival and Sligo Live festival. In 2016 she released her first solo album, Out of My Own Light, to great acclaim.

events.summary: Eivør Pálsdóttir is a Faroese singer, songwriter and producer whose genre-defying sound has captivated audiences around the world. Hailing from the village of Syðrugøta in the Faroe Islands, she weaves Nordic folk traditions together with dark electronica, rock and cinematic pop. Her extraordinary voice and emotionally charged performances have made her one of the most distinctive artists to emerge from the Nordic music scene. Over a career spanning more than two decades, Eivør has built a devoted international following through her recordings and immersive live shows. She has toured extensively across Europe and North America, sold out headline concerts and supported artists including Heilung. Her performances have also reached audiences at major events, including The Game Awards at the Hollywood Bowl and the UEFA Champions League opening ceremony. Beyond her solo work, Eivør is widely known for her contributions to \The Last Kingdom\, \God of War\ and \God of War Ragnarök\. Her music has earned critical acclaim and awards including the Nordic Council Music Prize, Icelandic Music Awards and multiple Faroese Music Awards. Her new album, \TUNGL\, arrives on 16 October 2026 via Nuclear Blast. Following the darker, atmospheric direction of \ENN\ \(2024\), the ten-track album explores the changing cycles of life through songs of tenderness, heartache, love, loss and renewal. Its title is the Faroese word for “moon.” Eivør will celebrate the release with concerts in the Faroe Islands and Reykjavík, followed by a North American headline tour in 2026 and a European tour in 2027. For more information, visit eivor.com.

events.summary: VALÉ is a fiercely talented vocalist and songwriter from Barranquilla, Colombia. By her early teens, she had found inspiration in American pop and R&B music, and began writing songs of her own. Influenced by some of her idols, VALÉ started to forge her own unique voice and point of view on the genre. She has spent time writing and recording in Los Angeles and Barranquilla, assembling a new collection of singles to be released throughout the year as a follow up to her EP, Early Emotional Tapes. VALÉ’s infectious melodies, catchy hooks, and standout vocals are bound to win fans from all around the world, establishing VALÉ as the leader in a new generation of Colombian pop artists. events.summary: Footballhead is a Chicago-based alternative rock band headed by Ryan Nolen. At its heart, the band is a vessel to toil forward through internal and external insecurity. It also serves the unrelenting spirit of new-millennium Midwestern youth, with MTV and skatepark dreams in the core of their memories. By blending pop structures with alt and emo sounds, Footballhead channels the frantic, dramatic, and anthemic to map the pressure points of existence. It’s outcast music, revitalized in search of a modern, blissful awakening. Nolen was a skate kid from the western Chicago suburbs; the one who only kicked it with older neighborhood kids. The punkish attitude of late-90s and early-aughts alt-rock galvanized Nolen, from the infectiously fun music down to the fashion. A teenage relocation to Palm Springs, CA coincided with Nolen inundating himself with all the music he could: Warped Tour, 411 videos, Limewire and the like. The Footballhead ethos comes from this comfort zone of pop impulses and raucous energy, carried by a DIY spirit that grants Nolen the autonomy to facilitate honesty and reflection. Joined by Adam Siska \(The Academy Is\), Liam Burns, and Robby Kuntz, Footballhead crafts supercharged rock songs like brief, open secrets. However weathered one is from their struggles and mistakes, this music offers unbridled fun as a reprieve, and salves for the shaken. These are your old friends inviting you in to commiserate, elevate, and believe.
events.title: Footballhead & Silverstein & Stand Atlantic & Story of the Year

events.summary: Do You Feel Anger? lives in the familiar world of water coolers, staplers, and office conference rooms — but Nelson-Greenberg's language quickly reveals something far stranger underneath. When Sofia, an empathy coach, arrives at a debt collection agency as part of a lawsuit settlement, she finds a workplace where toxic masculinity has so thoroughly warped the atmosphere that even the most basic concepts — feelings, empathy, basic human decency — have become alien and absurd. The play is laugh-out-loud funny, populated by an unusual cast of characters whose skewed logic and bizarre non-sequiturs mask something genuinely unsettling. What emerges from the sensitivity training sessions is not reform, but a portrait of how pervasive and deeply embedded the patriarchy can be — and how it distorts everyone it touches, including those trying to resist it.
events.title: PSU Theater Arts Presents: Do You Feel Anger?

events.summary: BombargoBombargo is a Canadian based international touring band that drops a vibrant splash of soul over their distinctive vintage-pop sound. Well known for bringing unrivaled energy to the stage with sing-along anthems, double-brother harmonies, and a powerful message that combined make for one of the most captivating live shows ever! Frontman Nathan Thoens passionate conviction and Jagger-like dance moves even impressed billionaire and music industry icon Sir Richard Branson, quoting I havent seen this type of energy since The Rolling Stones! and he would know, having personally signed The Rolling Stones to Virgin Records.The band began with lead singer Nathan Thoen and guitarist Spencer Chilliak after the two spontaneously met and drove 16 hours to attend Sasquatch Music Festival where they became inspired to start a band. The duo wrote their debut single Let It Grow during their very first writing session and as part of Bombargos debut EP Back on Main which would go on to be included in The Top 10 Best Saskatchewan Albums of 2015 by SaskMusic. This further inspired them to continue writing, touring, and release their first full-length album titled We Are Bombargo. The group has since evolved into a 5-piece touring band adding Nathans brother Anthony Thoen on guitar, additional brothers Matt and Sammy Folkersen on keys and bass respectively, and Niall Cubbon on drums.Bombargo went on to receive massive acclaim when pop star icon Taylor Swift added their 2018 single Mr. No Good to her Spotify Playlist titled Songs Taylor Loves alongside mega artists including Ed Sheeran, Camilla Cabello, and Kendrick Lamar. Being the only unsigned band on this star-studded playlist saw Bombargo featured on CBCs the Q, NME, Exclaim, Fashion, Noisey, People, and Billboard. This success was followed up by the release of their most successful single to date Oxygen which pushed Bombargo into the Canadian Hot AC Top 40 Charts for the first time in the fall of 2019. The band also made its US touring debut in late 2019 with their 33 date North American Dream Tour which kicked off with Bombargo playing the sold-out Roughriders Labour Day Classic Half-Time Show to over 33,000 people. The bands highly anticipated US debut at Hotel Cafe in Hollywood, CA gained heavy press coverage including a raving article in Billboard Magazine.---Bombargo VIP, In Spite Of Everything Experience:- Early Access to Venue- Acoustic performance and hang with the band.- Limited edition signed poster and VIP Laminate.- Photo with Bombargo- Early Access to MerchVIP UPGRADE INCLUDES A TICKET TO THE SHOW.--- Notes on Seating: Open seating, may be limited or standing room only. events.summary: 7pm doors, 8pm show All ages welcome Dev Lemons Dev Lemons has built a career by refusing to fit neatly into a single lane. Equal parts alt-pop artist, songwriter, comedian, and internet personality, she has cultivated a fiercely loyal audience through her sharp wit, fearless authenticity, and genre-blurring music that balances vulnerability with humor. Originally gaining attention through her viral online content, Dev quickly proved she was far more than a creator making music, she's an artist whose songwriting explores the awkward, chaotic, and deeply human moments that define modern relationships and self-discovery. Her music effortlessly shifts between infectious pop hooks, alternative production, indie textures, and emotionally raw lyricism, creating a sound that's as unpredictable as it is instantly recognizable. Across multiple releases, Dev has amassed millions of streams while continuing to grow an engaged fanbase that connects with her brutally honest storytelling and unmistakable personality. Whether she's writing about heartbreak, anxiety, dating disasters, or finding confidence in the absurd, her songs feel like conversations with a close friend who isn't afraid to say exactly what everyone's thinking. Beyond music, Dev has become known for her comedic voice across social media, where her sketches and commentary have reached millions of viewers. Rather than separating her artistry from her personality, she's built a world where both coexist naturally-earning a reputation as one of the most distinctive emerging voices in alternative pop. With new music continuing to push her songwriting and production into bold new territory, Dev Lemons is proving that authenticity, humor, and emotional honesty aren't mutually exclusive, they're exactly what makes her stand out. events.summary: Full Spectrum is a free exhibition of immersive art by Portland artists at Daydreamer Coffee & Public House in St. Johns, on view through December 29. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread.
