events.summary: Do You Feel Anger? lives in the familiar world of water coolers, staplers, and office conference rooms — but Nelson-Greenberg's language quickly reveals something far stranger underneath. When Sofia, an empathy coach, arrives at a debt collection agency as part of a lawsuit settlement, she finds a workplace where toxic masculinity has so thoroughly warped the atmosphere that even the most basic concepts — feelings, empathy, basic human decency — have become alien and absurd. The play is laugh-out-loud funny, populated by an unusual cast of characters whose skewed logic and bizarre non-sequiturs mask something genuinely unsettling. What emerges from the sensitivity training sessions is not reform, but a portrait of how pervasive and deeply embedded the patriarchy can be — and how it distorts everyone it touches, including those trying to resist it.

Escuche las entrevistas a panameños que comparten sus recuerdos y su punto de vista sobre La Invasión . A documentary on the memories of the U.S. invasion of Panama in mid-December, 1989. Civilians in Panama City prepared for the holidays while the U.S. launched an invasion to depose the dictator, Manuel Noriega. Mass destruction of civilian lives and homes took place. events.summary: “It might be the best video, and song, to come out of Austin in the first half of 2022”, Peter Blackstock wrote as he praised the opening track of Scott’s debut album “L.A.” writing for one of the only two print newspapers in the “Live Music Capital of the World”. Hailing from Houston, TX, by way of Nacogdoches, TX, the accidental musician Scott Strickland now calls Austin his home after residing in the great state’s capital for more than 9 years. After transitions from retail to teaching filmmaking at three colleges from Waco to San Antonio, Scott found himself laid off as a result of the pandemic. He used this moment as an opportunity, forcing himself to get extremely creative with how he pursued this second lease on life, music, and his newly-found relationship with God. A season of hard-fledged, messy introspection led Scott to chase the kind of music that connects truth, music, and the soul in the kind of way that can only be raw, honest, and vulnerable. Not pretending. Not accusing. As a result, he stripped down his Rock/Pop sound and regrounded the arrangement with a more folk-centered approach, getting back to basics with lush string arrangements to compliment his bright, colorful, and airy sound. Now, having collaborated with some of the greatest artists in Austin in one of the greatest spaces in the city, Scott is very proud to announce his most ambitious project yet - Strings Attached: The 1500 Sessions.

events.summary: Your monthly ritual... An invitation to come back to center. Our nervous systems are constantly taking in information. Between work, screens, notifications, responsibilities, and the general pace of everyday life, our attention is often being pulled in multiple directions at once—with very little intentional time to slow down and rest. This monthly nervous system reset is a dedicated space to do exactly that: support nervous system regulation. This immersive sound bath experience uses crystal singing bowls, chimes, oceanic textures, and other therapeutic sounds to gently guide your system out of the noise and stimulation of everyday life and into a deeper state of rest. For 75-minutes, there’s nowhere else you need to be and nothing you need to do. Simply get comfortable, receive the sound, and allow yourself to unwind. Think of this as your recurring monthly ritual to come back to center - a space to intentionally step away from the busyness of life, reconnect with yourself, and give your body and mind the restoration you're craving. Come as you are. Yoga mats, blankets, and props are available for your use, but please feel free to bring anything that will help you feel even more cozy & comfortable. These sessions are open to all; no prior experience is needed. About Kristi Kristi Littman is a certified sound healing practitioner & facilitation teacher whose heart-led approach blends nervous system awareness, intuition, and deep presence. Since 2019, Kristi has held space for thousands of people through community sound baths, corporate wellness, sound healing training, and 1:1 mentorship. She blends crystal singing bowls, chimes, and oceanic tones to create immersive soundscapes designed to soothe the nervous system and realign the body’s natural rhythms. She often weaves in meditation and breathwork, offering grounded, intuitive guidance that helps participants soften, release, and remember their own inner wisdom. Benefits of Sound Therapy: Deep relaxation & stress relief Release tension Energy cleansing & balancing Improved mental focus Enhanced meditation & mindfulness Emotional release Physical healing support Spiritual connection Improved sleep Enhanced creativity & problem-solving Moments of clarity Deep rest
events.title: RITUAL: Immersive Soundbath [Monthly Nervous System Reset] w/Kristi Littman

events.summary: A native of the Pacific Northwest, saxophonist Kareem Kandi is a performer, composer, and educator, in high demand for his talents both on and off the stage. Kareem is a versatile musician with strong roots in the traditions of Jazz, Blues, Classical and Funk, and has been performing throughout the U.S. and abroad for years, gaining attention from critics and audiences alike. While staying true to musical styles of the past, he also keeps an eye towards the future by composing original music as well as new arrangements of timeless songs from the great American songbook. Since 1996, Kareem has been performing both as a bandleader and as a sideman to enthusiastic audiences around the world at concert halls, festivals, and clubs. Over the years Kareem has performed, toured and recorded with some of the finest musicians in the music industry including: Pete Christlieb, Patti Labelle, Mark Elf, Ali Jackson, D’vonne Lewis, Bill Watrous, The Seattle Symphony, Mordy Ferber, Julian Priester, The Paperboys, The Northwest Repertory Singers, Thomas Marriott, The Tacoma Symphony, Alex Duncan, Frazey Ford, DJ Hapa, The Polyrhythmics, Bill Ramsay, The Staxx Brothers, Jay Thomas, The Sabella Consort, Greta Matassa, The Temptations, Hadley Caliman, The Four Tops, The Harry James Orchestra, Wayne Bergeron, and many others. Because of his musical diversity, his group, The Kareem Kandi Band has a sound that is fresh, innovative, and appeals to a wide variety of audiences. Growing up in the northwest with its vibrant music scene allowed Kandi the opportunity to study with, listen to, and perform with world class jazz artists residing in the area. Artists such as Tracy Knoop, Jay Thomas, Don Lanphere, Bill Ramsay, and Pete Christlieb had a large impact on Kareem early in his musical education. After finishing high school Kareem received a full scholarship to Olympic College in Bremerton WA where he earned an Associate in Arts and Sciences Degree. While completing his degree from Olympic College he received another full scholarship to attend Cornish College of the Arts in Seattle WA. Kareem attended Cornish and continued his music studies with many renowned jazz artists that served on the faculty at the time which included: Jovino Santos Neto, Julian Priester, Hadley Caliman, Dave Peck, Randy Halberstadt, Chuck Deardorf, and Jim Knapp. Kareem completed his Bachelor’s degree from Cornish in 2002 and since then has been very active as a performer, composer, and teacher. As an educator Kareem maintains a busy schedule teaching at The Tacoma School of the Arts as an artist in residence. He also maintains a full studio of forty private students, conducts weekly jazz classes at Ted Brown Music, and regularly conducts masterclasses and workshops at schools around the U.S. and Europe. Along with his teaching duties he is also the director of The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra, The Tacoma Jazz Association, and has served on the Tacoma Arts Commission. Kareem is a performing artist and clinician for Conn-Selmer and D’addario Woodwinds.
events.title: The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra

events.summary: Terry Robb Quartet-(Adam Scramstad, Dave Kahl, Gary Hobbs) Some musicians win awards. Then there are the very few who have awards named after them. Terry Robb – hailed as a blues guitar virtuoso and one of the finest acoustic guitarists on the international scene – is one of the latter. The Vancouver-born, Portland-based bluesman took home the Muddy Award for Best Acoustic Guitar so many times that the Cascade Blues Association finally broke down and attached his name to the trophy permanently. Recognition for his artistry doesn't stop there. The Oregon Music Hall of Famer has been praised by The Blues Foundation, Rolling Stone, Acoustic Guitar, Down Beat, Guitar Player, Vintage Guitar, Living Blues and Oprah’s O Magazine, extolling his talents as a finger-picker, singer, songwriter, arranger and producer. He's toured the country with Buddy Guy, Steve Miller, Robin Trower, and John Fahey, appeared on Late Night with Conan O'Brien, dazzled the crowd at Portland Trail Blazers games, collaborated with the Oregon Symphony, and had his work featured in Game of Thrones. During his multi-decade run in the spotlight, he's shown himself to be a master of nearly every blues style and technique imaginable. Robb's recordings have been praised by critics and musicians on the international stage. His original tunes draw on influences as varied as country blues to Coltrane, ragtime to Hendrix, and Americana to American Primitivism. His recordings are nominated, award winning and place high on prestigious playlists and recording charts. Said Dan Forte of Vintage Guitar magazine., “In Terry Robb’s hands, it not only makes perfect sense, it makes perfect blues sense.” Ty Curtis – One of the Pacific Northwest’s most compelling blues-rock voices, Ty Curtis delivers music with soul, power, and passion. A veteran performer with eight albums under his belt, he’s graced stages alongside legends like Robert Cray, The Doobie Brothers, and George Thorogood. His band—featuring Brian Harris (keys), David Kahl (bass), and Richard Lawrence (drums)—brings dynamic chemistry and seasoned musicianship to every performance. Their latest release, Ascendant Blues, marks a bold evolution in Ty’s sound—rich, raw, and resonant. Whether you're grooving to his guitar work or caught up in his emotionally-charged vocals, this is a show that transcends expectations. With accolades including multiple top rankings on Blues Rock Review and a standout 2nd place finish at the 2009 International Blues Challenge in Memphis, Ty Curtis continues to prove he's a force in modern blues. Richard Lawrence is a talented drummer known for his exceptional skills and musicianship, bringing a unique energy to every performance. He serves as the drummer and musical director for Ty Curtis, showcasing his versatility across various musical genres. Dave Kahl is a prominent blues bass player based in Oregon with decades of experience in the local music scene. He is recognized as a staple of Oregon blues, having played in many top bands in the region Drummer Gary Hobbs is a native of the Pacific Northwest and lives in Vancouver, WA. He has played professionally for over 4 decades and appears on over 60 recordings. Gary played with The Stan Kenton Orchestra from 1975 through 1977. Through the years Gary has played with Randy Brecker, Bud Shank, George Cables, Ken Peplowski, Pete Christlieb, Greta Matassa, Anita O'Day, Dan Siegel, Glen Moore, The New York Voices, Eddie Harris and many more. Randy Brecker, Bill Mays, Kurt Elling, Dave Frishberg, David Freisen, Bobby Shew, Bobby Watson, Bob Florence, Carl Saunders, The Woody Herman Orchestra,Terry Gibbs, Jaquie Naylor, Jim Widner Big Band, Stan Kenton Alumni Big Band and Tom Grant are just a few of the artists that Gary has recently performed with. Carnagie Hall, Royal Festival Hall, Tivoli Garden, Kennedy Center and Wolf Trap are among the venues Gary has played along with scores of festivals and clubs all over the world. Gary is very active in Jazz Education teaching at The University Of Oregon and traveling all over the US doing clinics, concerts and jazz camps with the help of Crescent Cymbal Company and Yamaha Drum Company.
events.title: Terry Robb & Ty Curtis

events.summary: In its third year, PAM CUT’s PLUS PLUS Festival of Tomorrow returns to celebrate unbound artists who dissolve boundaries, defy easy categorization and expand the notion of what’s possible in cinema and beyond. This world-class gathering in Portland amplifies and expands PAM CUT’s vision where storytelling, tech, media artists, and creative communities collide to explore new ideas and form new audiences charting fresh ways to move our world and ourselves forward. PLUS PLUS features wildly imaginative programming for cultural snackers, including unbound cinema, comedy, performances, sound-driven and interactive storytelling, live animation, and other media arts. Taking place November 19-22 at PAM CUT’s Tomorrow Theater, as well as at the Portland Art Museum, the festival is uniquely focused on active, participatory, experiential art and storytelling.2026 Festival highlights include: the Portland premiere of LIGHTSCAPE, by world-renowned multi-media artist Doug Aitken; a special live music/video game performance by Portland’s EMA; an evening of ‘90s “analogue ecstasy” hosted by music video legend and filmmaker Mark Pellington; a one-night-only evening of stand-up with Joel Kim Booster \(Loot, Fire Island\); and an afternoon with MacArthur Fellows and multi-hyphenate storytellers Sterlin Harjo \(Reservation Dogs, The Lowdown\) and Reginald Dwayne Betts in a spirited discussion on the nature of “truthiness.” New in 2026! PAM CUT introduces the PLUS PLUS Bizarre Bazaar, where a curated group of local and national media artists, publishers, exhibitors, community organizations, indie distributors, and creative collectives will gather to bring the idea of Plus Plus to life. Visitors will be able to browse and buy artist editions, books, comics, zines, physical media, prints, apparel, games, and connect with local and national artists, filmmakers, publishers, and organizations from across the independent, multi-media creative community. The market will be bustling with storytelling in its many forms, including live makeup demos and interactive gaming experiences, among other to-be-announced activations. The market will take place at the Portland Art Museum’s Fred and Suzanne Fields ballroom on Saturday, November 21, and will be free to attend.Tickets are on sale now at https://tomorrowtheater.org/plus-plus.

THE EXPERIENCE Part origin story, part healing spell. Decrepit psychedelia with a powerdrone score. Memory As A Rock Out Of Reach is a duet performance in which Erika M. Anderson \(EMA\) and visual artist Tabitha Nikolai use video game technologies to build out the psycho-sexual inner world of a girl-child in the '80s. Soundtracked by modular synth and guitar, a narrator searches for her shape amid commercial detritus, degraded 3D scans and a Polly Pocket apocalypse. This screening is part of our Plus Plus Festival. Check out the full program here ! ON STAGE: Erika M. Anderson & Tabitha Nikolai Erika M. Anderson is an artist and musician who has been active in the West Coast DIY and experimental scene for over two decades. She performs under her initials as EMA and has toured extensively, playing internationally in warehouses, sold-out arenas and everywhere in between. In 2011 she released her critically-acclaimed solo debut, Past Life Martyred Saints, which has been included on the "Best Of The Decade" lists from Pitchfork, Stereogum and Rolling Stone. Her albums are frequently self-produced, with a signature style that borrows from noise, folk and memories of popular music. While Anderson's music has brought her to prestigious music festivals, including Coachella, Bonnaroo and Roskilde, her multimedia performances have taken place in museums such as PS1 MoMA, The New Museum and The Barbican Centre in London. She has been profiled in The New Yorker, The New York Times, The Guardian and many others. NPR called her indie music's "greatest worldbuilder." Originally from South Dakota, Anderson now lives in Portland, Oregon, where she runs a recording studio. https://www.iwannadestroy.com/ Tabitha Nikolai is a visual artist and designer who uses video games, installation, and writing to study life under the visceral and disorienting onslaught of mass virtuality. Currently based in Portland, she grew up in Utah, and is forever influenced by her experiences there. Her work orbits themes of gender, isolation, futurism, and fantasy, often with a dark and humorous twist. With a long history of running DIY spaces, Nikolai believes deeply in the lifesaving power of community-organized scenes. Her work has been shown internationally at venues including the Kunsthall Trondheim, Trondheim, Norway; Vox Populi, Philadelphia, PA; and apexart, New York, NY. Nikolai's video games have been covered by The New York Times, VICE, and Art in America, and in academic outlets including the Journal of Gaming & Virtual Worlds. https://tabithanikolai.com
events.title: Memory as a Rock Out of Reach by EMA & Tabitha Nikolai

events.summary: Join us for a very special performance as Horse Feathers celebrates the 20th anniversary of their debut album Words Are Dead. To support the release, Horse Feathers’ current ensemble of Justin Ringle (guitar, vocals, banjo), Nathan Crockett (violin, saw), Halli Anderson of River Whyless (violin, vocals), Kati Claborn of Blind Pilot (banjo, vocals, clarinet), and Luke Ydstie also of Blind Pilot (bass, cello, vocals) faithfully recreate the mood of the original release with taut dynamics and sensitive arrangements. Revisiting the album now, with two decades of distance, reveals not just a beginning but a foundation. The same careful interplay, the same attention to space and tone, still anchors the band’s work today. In that sense, it feels less like a retrospective and more like a continuation. A reminder that some records do not age so much as they wait for the right moment to be heard again. In the years following Words Are Dead, Horse Feathers quietly built a body of work defined by patience and evolution rather than reinvention. Records like House With No Home, Thistled Spring, and Cynic’s New Year expanded their sonic palette without abandoning the restraint that first set them apart. By the time of Appreciation, the band had begun to open its sound outward, introducing richer arrangements and a subtle warmth that suggested growth without rupture. Through it all, Ringle remained a steady center, writing songs that favored emotional precision over spectacle. Kill Rock Stars is set to release a deluxe reissue that will be completely remastered and pressed on an exclusive vinyl color. It will include a replica of their original six-song demo CD in the package, along with a deluxe foil-stamped LP jacket. The reissue of Words Are Dead does not attempt to rewrite that history. Instead, it brings the origin point back into focus, offering a rare chance to hear where it all began while recognizing how far the project has traveled since.
events.title: Horse Feathers 20th anniversary tour

Jody Carroll performs old Delta, Country Blues, and American Roots music alongside striking original songs like no other. He stands among the most powerful Americana, Folk, and Blues songwriters and guitar masters on the scene today—a haunting improvisational shaman who conjures up the Delta dust one moment and the deep Delta mud the next. More than a consummate musician, Jody is an entrancing storyteller, weaving history, grit, and raw human emotion into every narrative he shares. Having spent formative years living and breathing the musical landscapes of the Blue Ridge Mountains and Nashville, his artistry is deeply rooted in American tradition. An award-winning artist with a formidable international touring history spanning America, Europe, and Japan, he has shared the stage with legends such as Buddy Guy, Johnny Winter, Honey Boy Edwards, and George Thorogood, among others. His live performances are a compelling, high-voltage mix of visionary original compositions and timeless interpretations from the American folk and blues traditions. Rich in absolute authenticity and magnetic stagecraft, every show delivers an unforgettable experience that commands the room from the first note to the last.

events.summary: Kalos is drawn to water. Every performance is like stepping into a river—they never play a song the same way twice. They make music inspired by the maritime traditions of Scotland, Ireland, Scandinavia and North America. Their album titles—Harbour and Headland—honor the meeting point between the land and sea and they sing songs about shorelines, seafarers and drownings. They revel in the driving danceability of Irish tunes, but also take inspiration from the pastoral melodies and naturalistic metaphors of Scottish music. But while the music they write is forged in tradition, it is nonetheless cast and tempered in new and unexpected ways. The trio spans three generations, three cities and two countries. Ryan McKasson \(violin, viola, voice\), Eric McDonald \(guitar, mandolin, voice\) and Jeremiah McLane \(accordion, piano, voice\) met over the years at highland games, contra dances and fiddle camps across North America. They made their first recording in 2016 and have been touring together since 2019. Kalos prizes the magic of live performance—breathing, dancing and weaving together like high-wire acrobats. They are as generous as they are virtuosic. Like nature itself, their music is full of chaos and chance yet always feels spacious and balanced. Their concerts are more an exposé than a performance—they are immersive, trance-inducing experiences. events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.
events.title: The Bylines

events.summary: SICK: A Year in Our Bodies Our bodies may be sick. Our lives are not over. Our stories deserve to be seen. SICK: A Year in Our Bodies is a fundraising showcase centering Portland-area sex workers living with chronic illness and disability---and the ways we have learned to survive in a world that wasn't built in our favor. For many disabled and chronically ill people, traditional employment demands something our bodies cannot always promise: the same energy every day, rigid schedules, eight-hour shifts, limited rest, and the ability to simply push through. Sex work can offer something different---the ability to build work around our bodies instead of constantly punishing our bodies to fit the expectations of work. We are dancers. Performers. Artists. Providers. Mothers. Hustlers. Creators. Disabled people. Chronically ill people. Survivors. This night brings our community together for performances, vendors, entertainment, and unapologetic visibility while raising funds for Rose and Pistolita to create SICK: A Year in Our Bodies---a calendar featuring 12 iconic Portland-area sex workers living with chronic conditions. Each month will put a real body and a real story behind invisible illness. Not as tragedy. Not as inspiration porn. Not as bodies to pity. As bodies that adapted. Bodies that worked. Bodies that survived. Bodies that are still fucking here. This project is about what survival actually looks like when your body refuses to cooperate with the rules of an able-bodied world. It is about the ingenuity of people who found another way when conventional systems failed them. And it is about refusing the shame that so often surrounds both disability and sex work. We are taking the bodies society tells us to hide---and putting them on the fucking calendar. Twelve workers. Twelve bodies. Twelve stories of adaptation, resistance, sexuality, illness, labor and survival. Come celebrate the people who learned how to make a living on their own terms. Come support chronically ill and disabled sex workers telling their own stories. Sick people are strong people. Disabled bodies are worthy bodies. Sex workers are workers. And survival deserves to be seen. SICK: A Year in Our Bodies November 21 • 8 PM • Dante's • 21\+
events.title: SICK: A Year In Our Bodies - Fundraiser Showcase

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.
events.title: refractiv Photography Exhibition

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. events.summary: From bayou kitchens to front porches, this captivating play celebrates the heart, humor, and resilience of Louisiana's women. Pull up a chair and savor a celebration of the remarkable women whose strength and spirit have always been the secret ingredient in Louisiana’s gumbo. This show is for you if you’ve ever wondered… Where do I belong? Where is home? What is a Cajun? What’s a Creole? Are they more than just styles of cooking? How different are Southerners from Northwesterners? How do you make a roux? What’s Mardi Gras all about anyway? What’s the deal with New Orleans and voodoo, vampires, and above ground graves? How do you “laissez les bon temps rouler”? Can you be both proud and ashamed of where you come from? How do you pronounce geaux, lagniappe, Ouachita, Tchoupitoulas, or couillon? Do you know what it means to miss New Orleans? Shelley Tate's one-woman show developed as an ensemble piece: a 90-minute show about history and culture of Louisiana —served with heart, humor, and just the right amount of spice. The gumbo is rich, the laughter is loud, and the women are unforgettable. THE EXPERIENCE Join us for a special screening of March Forth, a film about the poet, author, lawyer, activist, and 2021 MacArthur Fellow Reginald Dwayne Betts. Following the screening, there will be a moderated conversation with Reginald Dwayne Betts, Robe Imbriano \(Director & Executive Producer\), and Thomas Curtis \(Production Designer & Animator\). "March Forth Is a Beautifully Told Odyssey of Reginald Dwayne Betts's Life After Prison."- Black Girl Nerds "March Forth \(narrated by Oscar nominee Brian Tyree Henry \) conveys how powerful literacy and connection are, and how critical it is for the men and women locked up to not feel like they've been abandoned." - Honeysuckle Magazine The Partnership for Safety and Justice will provide information about their work before & after the event. This screening is part of our Plus Plus Festival. Check out the full program here ! ON SCREEN: March Forth 2026. Directed by Robe Imbriano and Valerie Hong. Runtime: 1 hour 35 minutes. Reginald Dwayne Betts went to adult prison at 16 and survived to write about it. March Forth is an intimate exploration into the life and thoughts of this acclaimed poet, author, lawyer, activist, and MacArthur "Genius Award" winner. Betts served almost nine years for carjacking, and before becoming an adult bore witness to the cruelties of the American legal system. In prison he named himself, "Shahid," meaning witness in Arabic. In solitary confinement, he became a poet. After his release on March 4th, 2005, Betts was determined to march forth into the world and leave prison behind. He began teaching, publishing multiple award-winning collections of poetry, a memoir, and even graduating from Yale Law School. As an attorney, he's secured the release of men he served time with. But instead of leaving prison behind, in 2020, he created Freedom Reads, a non-profit that places libraries he curates in prison cell blocks across America. The return has been complicated. Going back means remembering who is left behind and more painfully, those he's failed to get free. March Forth offers an intimate look into how he carries the two realities he moves through; one of immeasurable success and contribution and accolades and one of guilt and persistent doubt of his own self-worth. Through live performance, animation, poetry, and memoir excerpts narrated by Brian Tyree Henry, March Forth explores the lasting impact of serving time in adult prison as a teenager. ON STAGE: Reginald Dwayne Betts, Robe Imbriano, Thomas Curtis Reginald Dwayne Betts \(Subject \+ Writer\) Reginald Dwayne Betts received a BA \(2009\) from the University of Maryland, an MFA \(2010\) from Warren Wilson College, and a JD \(2016\) from Yale Law School. He is currently a PhD candidate in law at Yale Law School. Betts was appointed by President Barack Obama to the Coordinating Council of the Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention in 2012, and since 2018 he has served as a member of Connecticut's Criminal Justice Commission, which appoints state prosecutors. His additional publications include the poetry collections Bastards of the Reagan Era \(2015\) and Shahid Reads His Own Palm \(2010\) and the memoir Question of Freedom: A Memoir of Learning, Survival, and Coming of Age in Prison \(2009\). Robe Imbriano \(Director \+ Executive Producer\) Robe Imbriano is an award-winning director and showrunner. His animated musical documentary about the injustice of cash bail, " ," animated by Thomas Curtis with music and lyrics by Stew Stewart and Heidi Rodewald and published by The New Yorker, won Best Animated Short at the UrbanWorld Film Festival. He was the showrunner of the Hulu series, , with Colin Kaepernick. Imbriano co-created and Executive Produced the Netflix documentary series , starring Will Smith and featuring Mahershala Ali, Samuel L. Jackson, Sherrilyn Ifill, and Bryan Stevenson, to tell the story of the 14th Amendment and America's struggle with equality. He was a showrunner of the launch of , the very first major broadcast network series about Black life in America, nominated for 11 Emmy Awards in its very first season.Imbriano has written and produced for everyone from Diane Sawyer and Peter Jennings to Bill Moyers and Oprah Winfrey, winning numerous honors along the way. He currently runs the Documentary Specialization at the Columbia Journalism School. Thomas Curtis \(Production Designer \+ Animator\) Thomas Curtis won a Cinema Eye award for his work on Going to Mars: the Nikki Giovanni Project, seen on Max and shown at Sundance. He is a Motion Graphics artist and animator whose work ranges from the Annenberg Foundation's Constitution Project films, Right to Offend: The Black Comedy Revolution for A&E, CNN's New Orleans: Soul of a City , and Amend for Netflix. Recent projects include creating the design and animation for Criminal, a New Yorker Documentary about the harrowing conditions in the Harris County Jail. HOSTED BY: Partnership for Safety and Justice Partnership for Safety and Justice is Oregon's leading public safety and criminal justice reform organization. Together with advocates like you, we advance public safety solutions that invest in accountability and healing - not isolation and punishment - so that people can recover from trauma, families can safely stay together, and communities can thrive. events.summary: In Buddhist thought, the Tree of Life is a symbol of awakening, wisdom, and the interconnectedness of all life. Its roots reach deep into the earth while its branches extend toward the sky, reminding us that each generation grows from those that came before and that our lives are shaped by the communities and traditions that sustain us. Opening the PSU Choirs' concert season, "Tree of Life" explores these themes through music that spans continents and centuries. Performed by the PSU Chamber Choir, Rose Choir and Thorn Choir, the program pairs cherished works from the Classical choral tradition with music by a new generation of Southeast Asian composers. At its center is Indonesian composer Bagus Utomo's Gayatri, inspired by the legendary queen whose wisdom and spiritual devotion remain an enduring part of Indonesian cultural heritage. The concert also features works by Budi Susanto Yohanes, Ily Matthew Maniano and Matthew Lyon Hazzard. Several of these pieces will be recorded later this year by the internationally acclaimed PSU Chamber Choir at Skywalker Sound, offering audiences an opportunity to hear this music before it is released.
events.title: Tree of Life: Featuring the PSU Chamber, Rose and Thorn Choirs

events.summary: On Sunday, November 22, 2026, New York-based pianist, composer, and storyteller David Haney brings the world premiere of The Waters of Non-Existence: Vishnu to Portland, Oregon — an immersive concert work for piano, bass clarinet, bass, and spoken narration. The performance takes place at Augustana Lutheran Church at 4:00 PM and features two of Portland's most celebrated creative musicians: multi-reed master Ike Levin on bass clarinet and bassist Shao Way Wu. The Waters of Non-Existence: Vishnu draws on three ancient Vedic stories of the Hindu god Vishnu — the Preserver, the Dreamer of Worlds, the God who enters human life in moments of cosmic need — and reimagines them within a contemporary New York City setting. The result is an evening of music and mythology that contemplates what it means for the divine to live among us: in the streets, in the subways, in the silences between notes. The concert is drawn from Haney's new album, The Waters of Non-Existence, released in June 2026 on Ravello Records / PARMA Recordings — a work that has earned national press attention and critical praise since its release.
events.title: THE WATERS OF NON-EXISTENCE: VISHNU IN PORTLAND

events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: Time and again, great athletes seem to do the impossible. Their skills amaze us. Their work ethic inspires awe. Their talent is next level. At the same time, an athlete’s fame gives them a platform to speak out on important issues. With words and actions, a basketball star or Olympic legend can reach millions of people with their message. Jules Boykoff, Alex C. Davis, and Amira Rose Davis’s Athlete and Activist \(University of Illinois\) highlights sports figures who risked their popularity and even their careers to stand against injustice. Each profile takes readers inside the issues that motivated an athlete’s activism. Striking portraits by award-winning illustrator Martin French add a visual dimension to the dramatic stories. Throughout, the authors show athletes using different kinds of activism. Some spoke out. Others performed silent gestures. Still others let their success speak for itself. A different kind of sports history, Athlete and Activist is an inspiring look at heroic acts beyond our favorite games. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/boykoff-davis-davis-french-9780252059919
events.title: Powell's Presents: Jules Boykoff, Alex C. Davis, Amira Rose Davis, and Martin French

events.summary: In its third year, PAM CUT’s PLUS PLUS Festival of Tomorrow returns to celebrate unbound artists who dissolve boundaries, defy easy categorization and expand the notion of what’s possible in cinema and beyond. This world-class gathering in Portland amplifies and expands PAM CUT’s vision where storytelling, tech, media artists, and creative communities collide to explore new ideas and form new audiences charting fresh ways to move our world and ourselves forward. PLUS PLUS features wildly imaginative programming for cultural snackers, including unbound cinema, comedy, performances, sound-driven and interactive storytelling, live animation, and other media arts. Taking place November 19-22 at PAM CUT’s Tomorrow Theater, as well as at the Portland Art Museum, the festival is uniquely focused on active, participatory, experiential art and storytelling.2026 Festival highlights include: the Portland premiere of LIGHTSCAPE, by world-renowned multi-media artist Doug Aitken; a special live music/video game performance by Portland’s EMA; an evening of ‘90s “analogue ecstasy” hosted by music video legend and filmmaker Mark Pellington; a one-night-only evening of stand-up with Joel Kim Booster \(Loot, Fire Island\); and an afternoon with MacArthur Fellows and multi-hyphenate storytellers Sterlin Harjo \(Reservation Dogs, The Lowdown\) and Reginald Dwayne Betts in a spirited discussion on the nature of “truthiness.” New in 2026! PAM CUT introduces the PLUS PLUS Bizarre Bazaar, where a curated group of local and national media artists, publishers, exhibitors, community organizations, indie distributors, and creative collectives will gather to bring the idea of Plus Plus to life. Visitors will be able to browse and buy artist editions, books, comics, zines, physical media, prints, apparel, games, and connect with local and national artists, filmmakers, publishers, and organizations from across the independent, multi-media creative community. The market will be bustling with storytelling in its many forms, including live makeup demos and interactive gaming experiences, among other to-be-announced activations. The market will take place at the Portland Art Museum’s Fred and Suzanne Fields ballroom on Saturday, November 21, and will be free to attend.Tickets are on sale now at https://tomorrowtheater.org/plus-plus.
events.title: PLUS PLUS Fest

Through Jannings’s colossal performance, THE LAST LAUGH becomes more than the plight of a single doorman, but a mournful dramatization of the frustration and anguish of the universal working class. In Wuhan Clan Ain't Nuthin' ta Duck Wit, Bernice Ye reclaims "Wuhan" as a symbol of resilience and reinvention through razor-sharp stand-up, original comedy rap, martial arts, audience interaction, and cinematic multimedia. It's a show about identity, ambition, and building your own clan when the world doesn't hand you one. Part comedy special, part concert, and unlike anything else on the comedy circuit. Bernice Ye is an international touring comedian, comedy rapper, and taekwondo black belt known as "The Jackie Chan of Comedy" (The Stranger), with 400K+ followers and more than 100 million views online. Born in Wuhan, China, she came to the U.S. with $1,000 and a computer science degree from Peking University, built a career as a software engineer and technical program manager at Microsoft and Hulu, then walked away from tech for the comedy stage. It was the most unhinged sequence of decisions she's ever made. It's working. Press: Featured in the Wall Street Journal, Los Angeles Times, The Stranger, and Seattle Gay News.Festivals and awards: New York Comedy Festival · Bergamot Comedy Festival · Best of the Fest at the Burbank Comedy Festival, Laugh After Dark, and Nate Jackson's Super Funny Comedy Festival "She hypnotizes you. You leave lighter, louder, and with her songs stuck in your head." "High-energy and hilarious. Bernice keeps surprising you." events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Skeletons Out of the Closet: A Spooky Art Show

events.summary: Ever since the publication of his debut collection, The Man Suit, Zachary Schomburg's perfect little gems of poems have been enthusiastically greeted by readers and have inspired young writers and poets to take up the craft \(they've also inspired quite a few poem-themed tattoos along the way, too\). Wool Moon \(Black Ocean\), Schomburg's seventh collection and his first after a five-year break, is signature Schomburg: imaginative, absurd, tender, and charmingly funny. Schomburg has said of his poetry, "Mostly I want my poems to generate their own energy through confusion. I want my poems to confuse the reader. Not a confusion in a cognitive or narrative sense, but in an emotional sense." The poems of Wool Moon achieve this delightful confusion, turning the ordinary and the everyday on its head and finding light and curiosity in all they touch. Schomburg will be joined in conversation by Joshua Marie Wilkinson, author of Trouble Finds You. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/zachary-schomburg-9781965154274
events.title: Powell's Presents: Zachary Schomburg in Conversation With Joshua Marie Wilkinson

events.summary: Our Foundation series is designed for anyone new to the practice of improvisation and for those wishing to re-learn or deepen their practice of the art form's basics. We welcome people from all backgrounds, both creative and non-creative, so no acting or performing skills are ever required: just a desire to have fun, trust your instincts, and learn! Students should expect to learn: 👂🏼New ways of listening 🎁 The gifts of staying in the moment 📚 Telling spontaneous stories with others 👣 Thinking on our feet & trusting our instincts 👥 Quickly collaborating with others 👀 Identifying & using non-verbal communication 💪🏼 Discovering our strengths Why Take Classes With Us? Change Through Play's studio is founded on the belief that student progress only comes from providing clear instruction and feedback. We not only want our students to learn the core skills of improvisation, but we also want them to IMPROVE over their time with us. Because of that, we offer learning opportunities that students won't find anywhere else, including: A safe, nurturing, and supportive environment 10 students max per class, so each gets lots of attention Coaching and check-ins throughout each class Blackboard discussions, to help visual and analytical learners Closing every class with students recognizing their own wins Receiving highly personalized notes from your teacher, celebrating your wins during the class series & recommending skills to work on when you come back for another class with us. Participating - for those who wish! - in our student showcases Receiving and reviewing vids & pics from our showcase as keepsakes and learning tools

events.summary: Babe Haven is a queer punk band known for their riot grrrl attitude and nu-metal edge. Formed in Boone, NC by Lillie Della Penna and Naomi Poesel, the band creates anthems of empowerment and resistance brimming with raw aggression. With a mission to uplift femme, queer, and BIPOC voices, Babe Haven turns every show into a space of radical inclusion and catharsis. Babe Haven has been setting stages ablaze and selling out shows, quickly becoming an iconic staple in the modern punk scene, shared stages with the likes of Mannequin Pussy, Otoboke Beaver, Soft Play, Teen Mortgage, Pinkshift & Pollyanna. They have also appeared at popular tastemaker festivals such as L7’s Fast and Frightening Takeover, Punk Rock Bowling & Jorts Fest. Their sophomore album, Nuisance, showcases a bold evolution in sound—blending nu-metal, thrash, and punk into a visceral, genre-defying statement that cements their place as one of punk’s most vital rising voices.
events.title: Babe Haven

events.summary: Lloyd Jones is a consummate guitarist/singer/songwriter/arranger/performer/ bandleader. One of the most original artists on the modern day blues scene, Jones is, in the words of Blues Revue, "certainly worthy of greater recognition." The release of his first recording for Blind Pig Records, Love Gotcha, should bring him the national and international acclamation he deserves. Jones was born in Seattle into a musical family, which moved to Portland soon afterward. "I remember music was everywhere in our house growing up. My dad was playing Dixieland jazz records and trying to teach me to play trumpet when I was only five years old. My older brother played drums and showed me how. Then he took me to his band rehearsals and had me playing gigs when I was just 13. He took me to see James Brown in '64. You've got to imagine James in '64 - ouch! Then B.B. King, Buddy Guy, even Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhee - all this before I was out of high school. I was underage and totally mesmerized" Jones got deep into the blues and was the leader of Portland's most popular blues bands, Brown Sugar, in the early 70's. "We got to work with touring musicians in those days, like Charlie Musselwhite, George "Harmonica" Smith, the Johnny Otis show, Big Mama Thornton and Big Walter Horton. That's how we learned, and that's really when I first picked up the guitar. A lot of times these people would stay at our homes and teach us music and history. Some of them have passed now, so I cherish those memories. S.P. Leary, who was in Muddy Waters band and was playing drums with Big Walter at the time, leaned over to me as he was leaving town and said, "Man, I'm getting old. You gotta keep it alive. It's a struggle sometimes, but if you love it, you keep on struggling."' Through the years Jones would continue to hone his craft by performing with the likes of Albert Collins, Robert Cray, Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal, B.B. King, Dr. John, John Hammond, Etta James, Junior Wells and Buddy Guy, and many more music legends. In the 80's Jones joined forces with ex-Robert Cray singer/harp player Curtis Salgado in a band called In Yo' Face. "That was one fun band! Seemed like we all had the same record collection. Curtis really pushed me as a guitar player, and when he left in '85 to join Roomful of Blues I knew it was time to play my music." Jones knew what he wanted to say and how he wanted to say it. The Lloyd Jones Struggle started in 1985 as a vehicle for his songwriting. "I love a good story. Most of the traditional blues stayed with a shuffle or slow blues. Being a drummer I keep hearing the rhythm of the words all broke down funky and swamp-afied; nice and relaxed but kind of turned inside out." Jones made two recordings in the late 80's for Criminal Records: The Lloyd Jones Struggle \(1987\) and Small Potatoes \(1989\). They won over a dozen local music awards, as well as acclaim from national music publications such as Down Beat and Guitar Player, which in turn led to some extensive touring for the band on the Miller Beer Sponsorship Program. In 1993 Jones released his third album, Lloyd \`Have Mercy' Jones - Live! on the Burnside Records label. In 1995 Lloyd Jones recorded a highly acclaimed album for the Audio Quest label, entitled Trouble Monkey. Blues Revue named it, "not only one of the best albums of 1995, it is one of the best albums of the 1990's," while Robert Cray called it "the best damn record I've heard in a long time!" Vintage Guitar Magazine said, "Jones offers vocals that would make Sam and Dave smile and guitar work Steve Cropper would be proud of" and referred to his affecting vocals as "gritty as a dirt road and smooth as melting butter." Lloyd's songwriting was starting to be noticed as well, with Joe Louis Walker and Gatemouth Brown covering two of his compositions. Jones and his band have become a mainstay on the West Coast circuit, and have brought their tasteful, crowd-pleasing brand of music from New Orleans to Canada to the Caribbean, where Delbert McClinton witnessed a performance and remarked, "When I heard Lloyd Jones live for the first time in January 1999, it was like exhaling after holding my breath for fifteen years." It was such a typically memorable set at the Santa Cruz Blues Festival that led to Jones' signing by Blind Pig Records. Jones describes his soulful and intelligent fusion of funk, blues, and R&B as "storytelling with a Memphis groove." His latest CD, Love Gotcha, presents Lloyd's writing at its trenchant best. His songs have the quality that makes them sound as if they have been around as blues standards for years or they seem to have fallen out of some time warp from the golden days of R&B. His approach to the guitar is both economical and rhythmically sophisticated, with a style that can be as delicate as it is devastating. And Jones' accomplished guitar and vocal work are complemented throughout the recording by some of the funkiest horn-rhythm-organ arrangements around. Blues lovers everywhere are about to discover what Lloyd Jones' fans already know - one taste of his beguiling music and you're captivated. Lloyd's gotcha! Blind Pig Records A division of Whole Hog, Inc. PO. Box 2344, San Francisco, CA 94126

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: The Literary Arts Bookstore is pleased to welcome author Rebecca Handler to celebrate her new novel, In the Round. Handler will be joined in conversation by Selina Fillinger. About the book: Have you ever been dead certain that you’re being observed, that maybe your very existence is predicated on how others see you? A few minutes after she’s become convinced she’s the victim of a home invasion, In the Round’s brilliant and intimate narrator plunges us into a feminist Kafkaesque literary mystery that unfolds over the course of one weird—and dare we say, dramatic—night in San Francisco. Nothing is missing from her family’s home, but everything feels wrong. So begins a sleepless night of questioning, and a novel packed with the kind of astonishing twists that leave readers wondering: Is all the world a stage, after all? Over the course of the evening, theatrical elements creep in: a cast list, a prop list, an intermission. At once an avant-garde thriller, a meditation on motherhood and mortality, a full-throated endorsement of gut-level intuition, and a tribute to the rapture of live theater in a post-pandemic world, In the Round is a lively, inventive, and completely singular story.

events.summary: Sweetbitter meets Nomadland in Nikki Ervice’s Roadshow \(Astra House\), where we follow Annie as she leaves her NYC life of bartending and dancing to drive cross-country to Alaska to meet her dying mother. Annie is burning out. She performs at Club X as Dog-Faced Girl, a burlesque act in which she hides her face behind a dog mask. It’s the only way she can dance — her greatest love — while making enough money for rent. But when she receives an unexpected letter from her estranged mother, Vera, postmarked from the remote island in rural Alaska where Annie grew up, her world stops. Annie’s mother abandoned her when she was only a few days old. Her father, a stoic, workaholic aluminum welder and fisherman, insisted on keeping her mother’s identity a secret. But now, on her deathbed, Vera wants to meet Annie. And with her father recently passed, Annie knows it’s time to return home. So she borrows a Buick LeSabre and sets out on an exhausting journey through the Midwest into Canada. On the road, Annie sleeps where she can. Her attempts at stripping are unsuccessful and humiliating. Her money dwindles. She begins to steal gas. For a thousand dollars she agrees to dance for a bachelor party at a private lodge on a remote lake. After a delirious, dangerous night that she barely survives, she finally crosses the border into Alaska. Not long after, the LeSabre gives out. Half-broken but drawn on inexorably by the threat of Vera’s death, and a visceral call of her homeland, Annie abandons the LeSabre and hitchhikes to the end of the highway system, across the bay, to the island of her birth, where Vera awaits. Sexy and fast-paced yet deeply felt, Roadshow explores the power of passion, inheritance, legacy, and class, and the grueling, smiling work of the stage and the hospitality industry. Ervice will be joined in conversation by Kathleen Boland, author of Scavengers. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/nikki-ervice-9781662603655

events.summary: Shafty returns to The Get Down for their annual 2-night Thansgiving week run! Tuesday, November 24 Doors: 7:00 PM | Show: 8:00 PM Wednesday, November 25 Doors: 7:00 PM | Show: 8:00 PM What began as essentially a goof – a chance to throw down some familiar dancy beats and jam for whoever felt like listening - ultimately lit a spark under the off-the-radar powder keg of Phish fans in the Portland, Oregon music scene. More time was spent talking about the possibility of putting a Phish tribute together than actually practicing, prior to their first performance at local basement pub The Goodfoot Lounge, in February of 2012. Expectations for attendance were moderate at best, yet before the band played the first note, there was a line out the door, culminating in a jam-filled celebration of the music of Phish to an over-capacity crowd! The demand for a repeat was high, and Shafty was born. If there's a motive, it's to recreate the energy of a Phish show, with the attitude of playful band-audience interaction at the forefront and sharp musical skill acting as a behind-the-scenes glue to hold it all together. Classic Phish gimmicks are in full force: trampolines, megaphones, choreographed dances, vacuum cleaner solos, instrument switching, and the secret language are alive and well at a Shafty show. The band's songlist evolves along side Phish's growing catalog. Now at over 300 songs performed, the repertoire includes brand new Phish material such as Turtle in the Clouds, Say it to Me SANTOS, Mercury, The Howling and more! A notable "Story of the Ghostbusters" mashup made news on JamBase.com, and the usual hijinks of slicing, dicing, and unpredictably rearranging songs continues. It is not uncommon for the band to perform weeklies at The Goodfoot Lounge, where they'll perform for weeks on end without repeating a single Phish tune, thus providing a fresh concert experience for the diehards who attend week by week, while adding new material. These weeklies have helped create the telepathic musical chemistry between the band members, as well as providing the motivation to learn as many songs as possible to please the fanbase.
events.title: Shafty: Portland's Tribute to Phish (2 Nights - 11/24 & 11/25)

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours
events.title: Friends of Historic Forest Grove Museum & Library Open

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Skeletons Out of the Closet: A Spooky Art Show
