events.summary: The wizard activists of SPEWW are excited to invite you to the 2026 Yule Ball, on December 12th, 2026! The Yule Ball is an enchanted evening of well-mannered frivolity, celebrating our magical community and doing some good in the world! 2nd Task - Black Lake will be our theme for this year. We encourage all of our magical attendees to embrace the theme as you think about your Wizarding attire. This event will be 21+, with NO underage wizards allowed. We have some exciting updates coming this year for Yule Ball. Presale tickets will be on sale from July 24th @ 5:00 pm until September 13th @ 5:00 pm Magical Champion Feast $105 and Generally Magical $45 Starting September 14th @5:00 pm until December 6th @5:00 pm Magical Champion Feast $115 and Generally Magical $55. Magical Champion Feast tickets will have a most scrumptious plethora of yummy selections to feast upon. When the Generally Magical portion begin at 7:30 pm we will have a delicious selection of desserts for all to enjoy included in all tickets. (The house elves that help make this magical are very excited about this addition} There will be further announcements about new and fun activities to be included in our evening of "Well Mannered Frivolity" so please make sure you are following us on Facebook or Instagram. The Magical Champions Feast will begin at 6:00 pm and end at 7:30. Champions will select their table of choice in the ballroom. This is where you will enjoy your delicious meal and also find your Champions Swag. Make sure to coordinate with your Magical Friends if you wish to sit together. Generally Magical Ticket admission will begin at 7:30pm. New this year our Dessert Station will also begin at 7:30 for all of our Magical Attendees. Got a whole Quidditch Team to bring? A limited number of whole tables are also available. Whole tables include eight Champion's Feast tickets, as well as the option to name your table and decide where in the ballroom it will be located. Champion's Feast Whole Tables are $850. With a little dash of Geminio magic we can add 2 additional seats. This information will be included in your email when purchasing an entire table. In the weeks leading up to the Ball, all guests will be challenged to participate in the Triwizard Tournament, a real-world competition designed to test your bravery, cunning, determination, and creativity. The winner of the Triwizard Tournament will receive a special award at the Ball! This year, the Yule Ball is returning to the Mt. Hood Ballroom at the Sheraton Portland Airport Hotel. (An airport is a location where muggles gather to ride in large dragon-like flying machines, as they lack portkeys and broomsticks.) This venue features its own entrance, with bountiful and free parking, and lots of room for us to spread out in! Guests who like to dance into the wee hours will also be able to get discounted rooms at the hotel, so you won’t need to worry about apparition accidents or overcrowded Knight Buses. Returning to the same venue is also giving us the chance to really lean into transforming the space to make it as magical as possible. Expect some new wonders this year! SPEWW is an all-volunteer nonprofit dedicated to literacy, equality, and human rights. We stand with the Wizarding fandom and believe there is still good to be done in Harry’s name. We are committed to helping uplift and empower the transgender community as well as create safe spaces for all LGBTQIA+ people in the HP fandom. This year's Yule Ball proceeds will the Marie Equi Center, which aims to enrich the health of the trans, queer, intersex and gender diverse communities through trauma-informed care, culturally-affirming services and social justice advocacy.

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. Step into a holiday where tradition is turned upside down and inside out. ’Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a glittering, whimsical journey through Clara’s holiday eve. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. Sprinkle in the perfect amount of comedy, and a touch of theatrical spark, and you’ve got a show as enchanting as it is unexpected. With its blend of elegance, humor, high kicks, and holiday spirit, ‘Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a new holiday tradition in the making.
events.title: Can Can's 'Twas the Night Before Nutcracker

events.summary: Trio Subtonic is a groove heavy power trio out of Portland, Oregon that blends genre bending funk with slow burning underground soul jazz. Led by keyboardist Galen Clark, Subtonic explores a coalescence of rock, soul, funk and jazz that simultaneously draws in listeners and pushes boundaries. Trio Subtonic releases their 7th full-length album and first vinyl print, The Space Around You, on December 8, 2026. This is the group's first studio release in nearly ten years. On this album, the trio explores a more experimental and introspective side while retaining the groove heavy sound and dynamic arrangements that distinguish their earlier discography. Imagined as a collection of soundscape stories spanning the last decade, these songs evoke existential disquiet and the moodiness of attachment in a time of change. The Space Around You is an uncompromising exploration of weird sounds, infectious grooves, and the playful interaction of the trio instrumentation. Featured artists include West Coast VIPs such as LA's Nicole McCabe \(alto sax\), Seattle's Andy Coe \(guitar\) and Portland's Cyrus Nabipoor \(trumpet\).
events.title: Trio Subtonic

events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.
events.title: The Bylines

events.summary: Take a pause from the everyday and spend an evening connecting with yourself, the moon, and the people around you. Join Danie Rhodes at Breathing Room for a candlelit New Moon Ceremony. Through astrology, guided meditation, intentional ritual, and time in community, we’ll explore the themes of this moon and what they might bring up for you. No experience with astrology or moon ceremonies is needed. Just come as you are, bring an open mind, and make a little room for yourself. Together, we’ll explore: Moon & Astrology - Learn about the themes of the full moon and how they may connect to your own life. Guided Meditation - Slow down, settle in, and make space to listen inward. Intentional Ritual - Reflect on what you’re ready to release, what you want to nurture, and what you’re making room for next. Cards & Reflection - Work with oracle cards for personal insight, inspiration, and a fresh perspective. Crystal Intention - Connect with the symbolism and energy of crystals, and take a specially chosen stone home with you. Community & Connection - Share space with others in a welcoming, candlelit setting, with room for conversation, reflection, or simply being present. Leave with a little more clarity, a renewed sense of intention, and time well spent with yourself and your community. About Danie: Danie Rhodes is a certified Spiritual Wellness Practitioner, Holistic Health Coach, and Intuitive Tarot Reader with a deep love for astrology, the moon, and the ways we can reconnect with ourselves. Through moon ceremonies, she weaves together astrological insight, guided meditation, intentional ritual, tarot and oracle cards, and the grounding energy of crystals to create space for reflection, connection, and personal growth. Her gatherings invite you to slow down, set intentions, release what no longer serves you, and reconnect with your own inner wisdom in community.
events.title: New Moon in Sagittarius Ceremony

events.summary: At the height of the holiday season, a group of workers and their families discover that their wages are going to be cut. Together, they decide to fight for a better life. As the struggle drags on, they find joy and community through the music and stories of their different traditions….and of this new world they now share. Featuring early 20th century American classics, alongside songs and folktales from Eastern Europe, Italy, the Philippines, and the Latin American diaspora, Bread and Roses celebrates the tapestry of people who helped to build this country, proclaiming "We all deserve joy, We all deserve beauty!" Portland Revels' annual holiday Midwinter Revels production celebrates the winter solstice and the return of the light at the darkest time of year. Each season the production is set in a different place and time, allowing us to explore different cultures and music traditions, while grounding the show in our familiar rituals and themes.
events.title: Portland Revels presents "Bread and Roses"

events.summary: ⭐️ Single tickets go on sale December 15, but you can reserve your tickets now with a season subscription! ⭐️ Sylvia Ridge, Tennessee is known for one thing during the holiday season: their Christmas pageant. When Oralene, the guiding force behind the production suddenly passes away, the tight-knit group of women she left behind—known as the Silver Belles—must step up to save the show. As they fumble through rehearsals and face old wounds, they rediscover their voices, their strength, and their deep bond with one another. With twangy new country tunes, holiday classics, and plenty of Southern charm, "The Silver Belles" rings in the season with community and the kind of chosen family that helps us find our place—even when we feel a little lost. Book by Allyson Currin Music by Matt Conner Lyrics by Stephen Gregory Smith Based on an idea by Cathy Alter & Sandra Johnson On stage November 25 – December 20, 2026 Performances held at the Broadway Rose New Stage, 12850 SW Grant Avenue, Tigard, OR Title Sponsor: Harvey & Sandy Platt Show Sponsor: CTA Pathology

events.summary: A John Prine Christmas with Jenner Fox Band Saturday, December 12th @ 7:30pm Doors open at 7:00 pm www.jennerfoxband.com Ever wonder what John Prine has to do with Christmas? Ever wished the beloved songwriter had more to do with sleigh bells, eggnog, and Old Saint Nick. Well, in 1994 Prine released his 11th LP titled, “A John Prine Christmas.” The critics didn’t acclaim it much, but with titles such as “Silent Night All Day Long '' and “I Saw Mommy Kissing Santa Claus,” it’s still Prine at his lovely wry best, bringing Christmas home. We are proud to present “A John Prine Christmas” – a night of your favorite songs featuring folk troubadour and Prine scholar, Jenner Fox, with his all-star band. The evening will weave together Prine’s classic hits, his holiday themed songs, stories, and lots of singing along. Come prepared to laugh and cry and ho ho ho your way through celebrating a true American original. The Bellingham, WA based band features piano, electric guitar, bass, acoustic guitar, and rich vocal harmonies. $35 - Adults $30 - Seniors/Students $5 - Arts for All - Anyone with an Oregon Trail Card

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

Audiences are invited to tumble down the rabbit hole and enter a world of muchness, magic, and mayhem as Portland Panto Players presents its spectacular pantomime production of Alice in Wonderland, coming to Alberta Abbey Name from December 11-20, 2026. Alice in Wonderland - A Musical Panto is a fun, interactive, family-friendly holiday event filled with slapstick, witty dialogue, great music, dancing, and a few wink-wink jokes for the adults. Kids and adults will laugh, cheer, and have a wonderful time. Packed with laugh-out-loud comedy, colorful costumes, toe-tapping songs, dazzling dance routines, and plenty of audience participation, Alice in Wonderland brings the much-loved story to life with all the traditional ingredients of a great British pantomime. Whether you're a lifelong fan of pantomime or discovering its magic for the first time, this is a Wonderland adventure you won't want to miss! If you purchase 10 or more tickets as part of the same transaction, you can receive a $5 per ticket discount and reserved seating for your group. Before purchasing group tickets, email us at PDXPanto@gmail.com for the discount code. After buying, send us your reservation date, time, and ticket count, and we’ll reserve seating for your group. The Portland Panto Players are proud to be partnering with Girl Scouts for our show. If you are a Girl Scout troop or family contact us at PDXPanto@gmail.com to obtain a code for your discounted Girl Scout price.
events.title: Alice in Wonderland - A Musical Panto

events.summary: Artifact Artist in Residence 10th Annual Holiday Market Where: Showroom of Artifact Creative Recycle 3630 SE Division St Dates: 11/3 thru January 2026 \# of Vendors: 40 Theme: Vivienne Westwood Narnia Forty makers. One showroom. A whole lot of holiday magic. Think 70s Vivienne Westwood meets Narnia: a little rebellious, a little enchanted, and wonderfully weird. Wander through a wonderland of locally made treasures, from ceramics, candles, textiles, and glass art to beanies, body care, bolo ties, sunCATchers, card games, journals, apparel, kitchen must-haves, and all kinds of artful things for your home and everyone on your list. Come curious, shop small, and find something delightfully unexpected. Meet Your Maker Holiday Market Kick Off Party: Friday November 6th 2026 from 6 to 8pm (in conjunction with Division’s 1st Friday) Join us Friday, November 6, from 6 to 8pm for an after-hours shopping party at Artifact! Get first dibs on our Artist in Residence makers and their one-of-a-kind goods at Artifact’s Holiday Market. Makers will be mingling with shoppers, and everyone is invited! Live music from accordion player Robb Obbink and his fiddle partner from Too Loose Cajun Zydeco Band Warm winter drinks from the Riot Bloom Coffee cart Complimentary gift wrapping for your local-maker finds (donations welcome to support Project Lemonade) Raffle kick off and shopping wish lists passed out for Project Lemonade Live portrait drawings by Victoria Herstedt, the perfect personal touch for your holiday cards Community Giveback: Give a Little, Make a Difference, November 4 – December 15 We’re spreading a little holiday magic with a raffle benefiting Project Lemonade! One lucky winner will take home a gift basket featuring an item from each of our Holiday Market Artists in Residence vendors, plus an Artifact gift card. Raffle tickets are $5 each, and 100% of raffle proceeds will benefit Project Lemonade, supporting foster youth across Oregon. Want to give a little more? Artifact will also serve as a drop-off point for Project Lemonade donations from November 4 through December 15. Many of our staff have volunteered with Project Lemonade and have seen firsthand what foster youth need. Together, we’ve put together a wish list of items to help make the season a little brighter: Stuffed animals Books Makeup kits Jewelry Hair accessories Gloves, warm hats, and scarves Packaged socks and underwear Whether you enter the raffle, donate an item, or both, every little bit helps. Let’s make the holidays a little brighter for the kids who need it most.​

events.summary: Overview Tickets Parking & Directions Series Overview Slow down and savor the stories behind the cup. Hosted in one of Lan Su’s garden pavilions and led by the Tea Masters of Yun Shui Teahouse, Garden Tea Tastings invite our visitors to enjoy an exclusive, small-group exploration of traditional Chinese and Taiwanese teas. Each tasting is limited to 8 guests and features a seasonal selection of three thoughtfully chosen teas while introducing their origins, processing, brewing methods, and cultural significance. events.summary: About the event ReClaim It’s annual winter pop-up fundraiser, Holiday Shop 2026, is a celebration of local creativity and sustainable gift giving! Held December 11-13, 16-20 from 12-6pm in ReClaim It’s new location in NW Portland, this festive pop-up features art and gifts made from at least 80% salvaged or recycled materials by 70 local artists. You will find home decor, garden art, greeting cards, jewelry, clothing, and more, all lovingly crafted from repurposed treasures. Celebrate the holidays with purpose and creativity at the ReClaim It Holiday Shop, your one-stop shop for sustainable, handmade gifts. About ReClaim It Founded as a nonprofit in 2014, ReClaim It is the only organization in Portland with permission to glean reusable materials directly from the Metro Central Transfer Station. By rescuing these materials, ReClaim It is able to offer affordable, sustainable supplies to artists, neighbors, and DIYers to reuse, repair & reimagine. To date, the nonprofit has diverted over 1.4 million pounds of usable items from the landfill, embodying Portland’s values of creativity, sustainability, and environmental stewardship. ReClaim It Holiday Shop 2026 710 NW 17th Ave. Portland, OR 97209 Fri-Sun, Dec. 11-13 & Wed-Sun, Dec. 16-20 12pm-6pm
events.title: ReClaim It Holiday Shop 2026

events.summary: Every friendship has a fault line, and at Pairings Portland it runs straight down the bar. Owner Jeff has been a Star Wars guy his whole life. Rae would follow Star Trek to the edge of the known universe. So they settled it the way a wine bar would. Jeff picked five Star Wars characters, each a small reminder for getting through wild times: Han Solo, for remembering to be a rebel, and Rotta the Hutt, for not always listening to your parents. Rae answered each one with a Star Trek character, and both sides of every pair are matched to the same set of adjectives. That makes ten wines, poured in head-to-head pairs, so you can taste the debate and pick a side. It’s a one-week run of galactically inspired fun, and all ten wines are $50. Pairings Portland, 455 NE 24th Ave · Dec 7–13 · $30–$50 · https://pairingsportlandwineshopreservations.as.me/StarWarsvsStarTrek
events.title: Star Wars vs Star Trek Wine Flight

events.summary: At the height of the holiday season, a group of workers and their families discover that their wages are going to be cut. Together, they decide to fight for a better life. As the struggle drags on, they find joy and community through the music and stories of their different traditions….and of this new world they now share. Featuring early 20th century American classics, alongside songs and folktales from Eastern Europe, Italy, the Philippines, and the Latin American diaspora, Bread and Roses celebrates the tapestry of people who helped to build this country, proclaiming "We all deserve joy, We all deserve beauty!" Portland Revels' annual holiday Midwinter Revels production celebrates the winter solstice and the return of the light at the darkest time of year. Each season the production is set in a different place and time, allowing us to explore different cultures and music traditions, while grounding the show in our familiar rituals and themes.

events.summary: Skip the mall and make lasting memories right here on the farm. Santa will be making special appearances on select days during our Christmas Season (open November 20 – December 20) and you’re invited! Santa visits are donation-based. Contributions to Santa’s Workshop are welcome in person or online. Leashed pets are invited too! Pets may visit the farm during any Santa appearance, but they can only join Santa on his lap during our special pet-friendly day on December 19th. Santa & Mrs. Claus Schedule Friday, 11/27\* | 9:00 am - 4:00 pm Saturday, 11/28 | 9:00 am - 4:00 pm Saturday, 12/5 | 2:30 pm - 4:30pm Sunday, 12/6 | 9:00 am - 4:00pm Saturday, 12/12 | 9:00am - 4:00pm Sunday, 12/13 | 1:30 pm - 4:00pm Sunday, 12/19^ | 1:30 pm - 4:00pm \Mrs. Claus will be joining Santa at *every appearance except 11/27.* ^ People & Pet Day! Santa will be taking photos with people as usual, but this day is extra special for our pets. Pets are welcome in photos on any day, but December 19 is their chance to hop onto Santa’s lap! *Christmas Season Q&A ❓ Do we need tickets or reservations?* ➡️ Nope! Admission to the farm is complementary during the Christmas Season. *❓ Is there a fee or cost to visiting Santa?* ➡️ Santa visits are free but donations are welcome and appreciated! You can thank Santa by contributing any amount you’d like to help keep the elves stocked with hot chocolate, eggnog, and supplies while they’re busy in the workshop. Your generosity also helps support charitable appearances throughout the season. Donations can be made in cash or online. *❓ Can we bring our own camera?* ➡️ Please do! Bring your own camera or phone to capture your photos. *❓ What time should I arrive?* ➡️ You’re welcome to arrive anytime during open farm hours (9 AM – 5 PM). Santa’s line will close at the posted end time, so be sure to join the line early to secure your spot. Once the line is closed, no new guests will be able to join the line. *❓ What else can we do at Frog Pond Farm this season?** ➡️There’s so much to enjoy during the Christmas season at Frog Pond Farm: Visit and feed over 80 animals Shop our holiday store for pre-cut trees, wreaths, garland, and local gifts Warm up by the bonfire and grab a festive drink from our coffee cart Drop a letter in the North Pole Mailbox Enjoy the farm’s cozy holiday atmosphere with friends and family (our bounce park is not open during the Christmas season) 📍 Frog Pond Farm – Wilsonville, Oregon 🕒 Open Fridays, Saturdays & Sundays | 9 AM – 5 PM 🎅 Visit schedule, FAQs, and more: www.thefrogpondfarm.com/christmas 💚 Come make your Christmas memories where the magic feels real, right here on the farm!

events.summary: Every Christmas Story Ever Told \(And Then Some!\) By Michael Carleton, James FitzGerald, and John K. Alvarez Directed by Mandy Khoshnevisan Three actors. 90 minutes. Every Christmas story ever written. What could possibly go wrong? Michael Carleton, James FitzGerald, and John K. Alvarez's gloriously unhinged Christmas comedy is exactly what it sounds like; A Christmas Carol. Rudolph. It's a Wonderful Life. The Grinch. All of it, and more, crammed into a single evening by three increasingly desperate performers who absolutely, without question have bitten off more than they can chew. Rapid-fire parody, breakneck costume changes, and a festive frenzy that is Bag&Baggage doing the holidays the only way we know how: hilariously. Whether you love the holidays, love laughing at them, or both, this one's for you. Discounted Preview Performance: December 3rd. events.summary: ⭐️ Single tickets go on sale December 15, but you can reserve your tickets now with a season subscription! ⭐️ Sylvia Ridge, Tennessee is known for one thing during the holiday season: their Christmas pageant. When Oralene, the guiding force behind the production suddenly passes away, the tight-knit group of women she left behind—known as the Silver Belles—must step up to save the show. As they fumble through rehearsals and face old wounds, they rediscover their voices, their strength, and their deep bond with one another. With twangy new country tunes, holiday classics, and plenty of Southern charm, "The Silver Belles" rings in the season with community and the kind of chosen family that helps us find our place—even when we feel a little lost. Book by Allyson Currin Music by Matt Conner Lyrics by Stephen Gregory Smith Based on an idea by Cathy Alter & Sandra Johnson On stage November 25 – December 20, 2026 Performances held at the Broadway Rose New Stage, 12850 SW Grant Avenue, Tigard, OR Title Sponsor: Harvey & Sandy Platt Show Sponsor: CTA Pathology

THE EXPERIENCE If you love Christmas, then why don't you merry it?! Ring in the season with our annual holiday tradition: the Pee-wee's Playhouse Christmas Special on the big screen! Packed with guest stars, queer icons, music, and Pee-wee's signature kooky cheer, this yuletide classic is pure joy. ON SCREEN: Pee-wee's Playhouse Christmas Special 1988. Directed by Wayne Orr & Paul Reubens. Runtime: 49 minutes. Rated PG. Pee-wee Herman and pals are celebrating Christmas in the Playhouse in their own creative ways: Pee-wee makes a list for Santa Claus 1 1/2 miles long, teaches Little Richard how to ice skate, goes for a sleigh ride with Magic Johnson, commands Frankie Avalon and Annette Funicello to make Christmas cards, receives a long phone call from Dinah Shore, even has more musical fun with k.d. lang, the Del Rubio Triplets and Charo! Finally, Big Red arrives and announces that Pee-wee's Christmas list was so big, he didn't have enough presents for all the children of the world. Will Pee-wee follow his own advice and help others? F

events.summary: Advance Tickets $20 HERE, Day of Show $25 Doors open at 1:30pm, all ages Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band If you’ve never heard French Louisiana-style dance hall music, you’re in for a real treat. And if you have, welcome back y’all! For more than twenty years, the Portland-based Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band has been playing their infectious brand of dance music from Southwestern Louisiana — at festivals large and small, parties, street fairs, and weddings throughout the Pacific Northwest. Take a great electric band, add two fiddles, an accordion, and a traditional rub-board, and you have an irresistible sound: happy, exciting, and exceptionally rhythmic. You won’t be able to sit still, guaranteed. Their repertoire includes Cajun, Zydeco, and New Orleans-influenced music, with male and female vocals (and harmonies), and lyrics sung in English and Cajun French. For you dancers, there are two-steps, a few waltzes, and a surprise or two. So come on down (and bring your dancin' shoes).
events.title: Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band-MATINEE!

events.summary: Young the Giant’s Victory Garden is an ode to radical empathy. The result is a prolific record that beckons a new era of creative fertility for the band and presents Young the Giant as confident, refined, and fully inhabiting its voice.

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. events.summary: Dead Pioneers vocalist, nationally known Indigenous artist of the Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe, Gregg Deal, started this project as an extension to a performance piece titled “The Punk Pan-Indian Romantic Comedy”. With the intent to create original music for this performance piece, the Dead Pioneers was born! Working closely with guitarist Josh Rivera and drummer Shane Zweygardt, Gregg tried to form something over the Covid lockdown. Original music from Shane and Josh got things flowing, but things clicked when Gregg met Lee Tesche, lead guitarist for Algiers, at an art residency in Florida and became Dead Pioneers bassist. The Dead Pioneers first single Bad Indian was born! Heavily influenced by Gregg’s Indigenous voice, this gave enough information to begin forming songs and the overall sound of Dead Pioneers. Later adding guitarist Abe Brennan to the crew while recording their first self-titled LP at The Blasting Room in Fort Collins, CO. Dead Pioneers is rooted in creating and performing a sound heavily influenced by the punk aesthetic with an edge built on a First Peoples perspective and not afraid to tackle hard political and social issues, standing in solidarity of Indigenous rights, Black rights, Brown rights, Asian rights, Gay rights, Trans rights, Workers rights and beyond. From original songs to spoken word with punk riffs, Dead Pioneers was created with a love of music, a love of art, love of a scene that saves lives as well as the DIY disposition of just figuring it out and seeing what happens.
events.title: dead pioneers

events.summary: Formed in 1995, Save Ferris remains one of the seminal and most beloved bands from the third wave of ska. The group’s Orange County home was fertile ground for a thriving music scene, with punk, rock, and ska emerging from the region. Save Ferris blended the best elements of these sounds and their humble beginnings saw them play house parties and local venues, powered by Monique Powell’s high-octane vocals. When KROQ DJ Rodney Bingenheimer played their cover of Dexy's Midnight Runners “Come on Eileen” on his show, the response was overwhelming and was added to the taste-making station’s playlist. All of this happened independently without a record label and with Powell serving as the singer and band manager. Save Ferris signed with Epic Records in 1997, unleashing their debut album, It Means Everything, and touring the world for the next six years. In 2003, SF went on hiatus until Powell, with a new cast of characters, reformed SF in 2013, coming home to Orange County and a sold-out show at the Pacific Amphitheater in Costa Mesa. Another raucous show at the Santa Monica Pier drew over 20,000 people, proving that the band wasn’t just back, but ready to roar. Powell is the centerpiece of the action. Her dazzling on-stage presence continues to wow audiences and the band’s energy is infectious. After spending 2023 touring and delighting fans, she is currently at work on new Save Ferris music for release in 2024. Save Ferris are out to prove their best days are still ahead of them.
events.title: Save Ferris

events.summary: Childhood friends, Ruby Haunt \(fka Haunt\) is an american musical project conceived by Wyatt Ininns and Victor Pakpour sometime in 2015. The duo wrote their first three EPs while in school via opposite ends of the west coast \(Los Angeles and Portland\), exchanging musical ideas over email. In this time they received support from Nowness, Track \+ Field Records, C-Heads Magazine, and various tastemaking YouTube channels for their unique songwriting and self-produced music videos. In 2016 the boys saw a move to L.A. where they wrote their debut LP ‘Sugar’, their first written together in a small ocean front house in Laguna Beach, California. ‘Sugar’ was self-released in October 2016, featuring collaborations with the renowned photographer Henrik Purienne, and film duo Wissa for their Roberto Cavali campaign in Vogue Italia. 2018 sees the duo busy at work on their next album and a live show that will tour towards the end of the year.

events.summary: Always on the go as one of the Pacific Northwest’s most trusted guitarists, Chance Hayden has performed avidly since the mid-00s as a chameleon-like musician who fluidly adapts through jazz, blues, funk and soul. He continuously splits duties as both a bandleader and avid sideman for diverse acclaimed artists such as Farnell Newton, Darrell Grant, Saeeda Wright, Shelly Rudolph, Lloyd Jones, Mel Brown and Jarrod Lawson with whom he toured 15 countries. Hayden's albums Get Somethin’ \(2018\) and Grab & Go \(2020\) were followed by the stand-alone single Shag Bag \(2022\) featuring iconic keyboardist Ronnie Foster of 70s-era George Benson fame. Most recently, Hayden centered his creative focus around the seldom heard baritone guitar with Baritone Gold \(2024\), showcasing a dozen 60s-inspired originals that span from surf to soul-blues with classic soundtrack vibes. Hayden’s works have been featured in television and film, including the Sony Pictures \#1 box office hit The Perfect Guy, the award-winning BET series Being Mary Jane and the popular Netflix series The Waterfront.
